workPackages.title: Lead step before wave 3: baselines and guards, the v2 contracts (additive), root configuration, boundary rules, reference images
workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: docs/MIGRATION_V2.md sections 1, 3 (the lead steps) and 4 (the contracts, file by file), ARCHITECTURE sections 2, 3, 5.4, 6.3, 7.2, 8.3, 9.2, 9.3, 13.3, 17.1, 18.8, 21, 23, 31.3, docs/research/v2/codebase-audit.md, every wave-2 hand-off.

THIS IS THE LEAD'S OWN STEP (v1 had lead-baseline). It runs alone, on a tree where wave 2 is committed, and nothing else starts until it is reviewed. It changes no behaviour: when it ends, every existing suite passes exactly as before.

SCOPE:
1. Swap the documents in (MIGRATION_V2 section 2), including PACKAGE_RULES rule 13d (22 GB baked, 20 GB packs, 25 GB free) and rule 8 (new test directories).
2. Baselines on the unmodified tree: the mission state hash; tests/mission/baseline-v1.json with the milestone states the tick-grid step will be compared against (orbit elements at every milestone, touchdown and splashdown positions, event times); unit and browser suite results; the summed GPU budget table.
3. Reference images (ARCHITECTURE 31.3): a PNG of every checkpoint in deterministic mode (frozen presentation time, streaming idle, fixed site-data snapshot) into data/baselines/ (git-ignored), a tracked manifest tests/browser/baselines.manifest.json (file, sha256, tolerance), and compareToBaseline(page, name) in tests/browser/harness.ts reporting mean absolute difference and the 99.9th percentile against the checkpoint's tolerance. Record each twice; the tolerance is at least three times the difference between the two recordings.
4. Terrain guard: heights from the real TerrainProvider at 2,000 fixed directions on Earth and on the Moon (bit-exact, band-limited and collision queries), and a hash summary of every tile directory, under tests/unit/terrain-core/terrain-guard.*; a test compares them.
5. Contracts, ADDITIVE (MIGRATION_V2 section 4 is the list): new files session.ts (FlightSession, LocalSession, UniverseCommands, ClientStores, PlanningService), vehicle.ts (VehicleCapabilities, Issue), net.ts (UniverseRules with every number of ARCHITECTURE 5, 7.4-7.6, 9.4, 15.5 and 26 as a field with its default and its timer base; ClockState, TimeView, CensusEntry, TargetRef, the view models; NO wire messages: wire-protocol writes that section in wave 4; no chat flag); new fields in sim.ts, controls.ts, defs.ts, simInternal.ts, render.ts, ui.ts, audio.ts, testApi.ts, terrain.ts (TileSourceSpec). Fields the sweep retires (SimSnapshot.tick, Readouts.targetBodyId and targetClosestApproach, LaunchSiteDef.pad, padAzimuthDeg, structures, the pause action) get @deprecated and stay. New required snapshot fields get neutral producers in World and in FakeSim in the same commit (as the lead you may touch src/sim/world and src/core/fakes for that and nothing else there), so the tree compiles and behaves as before. Doc-comment every field. src/core/math/frame.ts with the rebase helpers and tests.
6. Root configuration (nobody else may edit it): vitest include gains tests/universe, tests/load, server, bots (and tests/net behind NET=1, like MISSION=1); a Playwright project acceptance with testDir tests/acceptance; tsconfig.node.json (no DOM lib) covering server, bots, deploy and the headless src directories, run by npm run typecheck; a CI-only build script that writes outside the shared dist/; .gitignore entries for data/packs, data/baselines and data/stack; the script stack in package.json (npm run stack runs node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=stack -- node deploy/local/stack.mjs, which platform-delivery writes; until it exists the script prints that; the launcher is the wrapped command, so the slot is held for as long as a stack is up, and npm run stack -- [options] -- <command> runs a suite inside it); THE PAGE A BROWSER LOADS ON THE STACK (ARCHITECTURE 16.4): the script stack:client (a production client build with the same Vite configuration as the CI build, written to data/stack/client/<source hash>/, never to dist/, run under --class=cpu, a no-op when the hash of the client sources is unchanged: the only client build a package may run), the dev server serving /endpoints.json from the file named by STACK_ENDPOINTS (a 404 without it, so the app offers Practice only, as today), and tests/browser/globalSetup.ts starting no server of its own when STACK_URL is set and pointing the functional and acceptance projects at it (unchanged behaviour without it); the dependencies wave 3 needs (an S3 client and presigner for tools/pack and deploy; embedded-postgres pinned to PostgreSQL 18, and pg with its types, for the local stack of ARCHITECTURE 16.4), installed once on a quiet machine.
7. tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts: rules for src/universe, src/session (headless list), src/net (src/core only), src/client (src/core, src/sim, src/net; never src/universe, src/session, server), src/shell, src/bench, src/gate (no imports), server/ and bots/ (never src/render, ui, map, shell, audio; the client entry never reaches server/, bots/ or src/universe except through src/session), src/sim never importing src/universe, src/session or src/client. tools/dev/heavy.mjs gains --class=stack (ONE slot shared by the local stack and the docker compose suites of ARCHITECTURE 16.4, so the two never run together and never twice). THE SLOT MODEL IS FIXED HERE: heavy.mjs frees a slot when the wrapped command exits, so the stack launcher is the wrapped command and holds the slot for the stack's whole life; there is no background mode; a second launcher waits; a dead launcher's slot is reclaimed like any other; --status shows the holder. At a moment when no WSL workload runs, write the Docker VM cap of ARCHITECTURE 16.4 (memory 6 GB, 8 processors, 2 GB swap, autoMemoryReclaim=dropCache) into .wslconfig in the user profile directory, run wsl --shutdown, and tell the user (OPEN_QUESTIONS, Small things); do not start the Docker daemon. A repository scan tools/dev/check-stubs.mjs (TODO, FIXME, stub, placeholder outside data for the simple bodies) with an allow-list file.

ACCEPTANCE:
- npm run typecheck (both configurations), the unit suites, the functional browser project and npm run test:mission pass with the same results as the recorded baseline; the golden hash is unchanged.
- The boundary test fails on a planted violation of each new rule; the stub scan fails on a planted TODO.
- Every reference image compares clean against itself on a third capture; the manifest lists every checkpoint of 31.3.
- A test file dropped into each new test directory is collected by the stated command (then removed).
- With STACK_URL set, globalSetup starts no dev server and the functional and acceptance projects use that URL; without it nothing changes; npm run stack:client run twice builds once and writes nothing under dist/; a command wrapped in --class=stack holds the slot until it exits and a second one waits.
- docs/handoff/lead-baseline-v2.md lists the deprecated fields for the sweep, the island API and navigation signatures to be signed off before wave 4, and the exact commands of every guard.
SELF-VERIFY: npm run typecheck; node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=cpu -- npx vitest run; node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=cpu -- npm run test:mission; node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=gpu -- npx playwright test --project=functional.

RULES (docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, binding): (1) Edit only your owned paths; an entry starting with '!' is excluded. A change you need elsewhere is a request file in docs/requests/. The lead owns src/core/contracts (except the parts a brief names), the root configuration (package.json, the lockfile, tsconfig*.json, vite.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, playwright.config.ts, .gitignore), tools/dev, src/core/math, src/core/testing, labs/template and tests/browser/{harness,globalSetup,chromeArgs}.ts. Never run npm install: the dependencies and configuration entries you need are listed under PROVIDED BY THE LEAD in your brief, or are a request. (2) No placeholders, stubs, TODOs or silent fallbacks (CI scans for them); what cannot be finished is stated in the hand-off. (3) Engine code never names a specific body, vehicle, part, site, scenario or rule value; every number of the time model, pads, docking, expiry and rate limits is a UniverseRules field. (4) Headless code (src/sim, src/universe, src/session, src/terrain, src/pilot) uses no DOM, WebGPU, timers, Date, performance, Math.random, sockets or storage; npx vitest run tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts stays green. (5) Shared tree: verify with scoped commands only (npm run typecheck:paths -- <paths>; npx vitest run <paths>; npx playwright test <dir>); never npm run build or npm run check; every heavy command through node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=<cpu|gpu|bake|stack> -- <command>, one at a time; the only client build you may run is npm run stack:client (the lead's; it writes under data/stack, never to dist/); THE LOCAL STACK (host Node processes and an embedded Postgres 18, no Docker; ARCHITECTURE 16.4) NEVER RUNS IN THE BACKGROUND: start it only as npm run stack -- [options] -- <your suite command> with STACK_NAME=fsp-<package id> (the script takes the ONE stack slot of heavy.mjs, brings the stack up, runs your command with STACK_URL and STACK_ENDPOINTS set, and stops the stack when the command exits; a command inside it that needs the GPU is itself wrapped in heavy.mjs --class=gpu); hold the slot for one suite at a time and release it between suites, because other packages wait for it; the docker compose form (the pinned Linux image) is the same command with --compose, in the same slot, only for the suites your brief names, and it stops what it started, a Docker daemon included; never leave a server, database, browser or container running. (6) Git: only git add <your paths>, then commit; never add -A, stash, reset, rebase, amend or push (releases are tags the lead moves); commit working states often. (7) Write files with the Write tool, absolute paths. (8) Secrets (.env, provider tokens) are read only at run time by tools under tools/, server/, bots/ or deploy/; never printed, committed, logged in a URL or shipped to the client; run node tools/dev/check-secrets.mjs before every commit if you touch them. (9) Cloud: never touch existing Modal apps or volumes or the existing Railway project; create cloud resources only when your brief names them, only in the Railway project fable-space-program and the Modal environment fsp (both approved by the user: docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS_V2.md, Answered), on the Railway HOBBY plan and inside the stage-0 limits of ARCHITECTURE 16.2; anything that needs the Pro plan, raises the standing spend or is a rehearsal beyond what the Hobby plan allows is the lead's to announce to the user first: stop and ask the lead. Never build alert routing and never ask for a webhook. Everything else is built and verified on the local stack, which needs no cloud resource; never report a local-stack result as a deployed or measured-capacity result. (10) Browser work: real Chrome, real GPU, assert the adapter, close loops on state, LOOK at every screenshot you save; perf only under the GPU lock; where your brief names reference images, compare with the helper in tests/browser/harness.ts and never re-record one yourself. (11) Disk: data/ stays under 22 GB, data/packs under 20 GB, at least 25 GB of the disk free; delete intermediates. (12) Finish with docs/handoff/<package id>.md: public API with exact signatures, how to run and verify, measured numbers against every acceptance criterion (say plainly which were not met and why), known limits, and every contract change you request.

workPackages.brief:

You own the headless side this sub-wave; the presentation code (src/render, ui, input, camera, map, audio, src/app, labs, tests/browser) is NOT yours and is swept by presentation-sweep after you. The contracts are already written by the lead: new fields exist beside deprecated ones, so presentation keeps compiling while World fills both. For the site-id rename only (step 6) you may make ONE mechanical commit that replaces the old id in labs/ and tests/ files you do not own.

SCOPE, strictly in this order (MIGRATION_V2 steps 3.1-3.6; one step per commit series, each green):
1. THE TICK GRID, ALONE. v1's clock is off the v2 grid: lunar-direct starts at 938240818.839663 s (times 120 is not an integer; the QA scenarios too) and every advanceRails re-bases the step grid at an arbitrary float instant (src/sim/world/sim.ts: this.ut = target; this.utBase = target; this.stepsSinceBase = 0). Change only that: tools/sim/findStartTime.ts emits tick-aligned instants, start-time.json and the scenario and QA starts are snapped to a tick, rails advances and warp exits land on whole ticks (the event instant keeps its float second inside the tick for the SOI hand-over), ut = tick / 120 everywhere. Compare the mission against tests/mission/baseline-v1.json BY TOLERANCE (orbit elements at each milestone to 1e-6 relative, touchdown within 50 m, splashdown in the same recovery zone, event times within 1 s), then re-baseline the golden hash (re-baseline 1). Nothing else changes in this step.
2. Trajectory guard, recorded on the tick-grid tree: tests/mission/trajectory-guard.json (body-centred position, velocity, attitude, mass of the ATTENDED craft of lunar-direct at 400 sample ticks) and tests/unit/sim-vessel/trajectory-fixtures (ascent, staging, entry, touchdown, splashdown, lunar ascent), compared bit-exact; debris of the mission is recorded by fate (impact or decay tick and position, or final orbit) and compared within 2 s and 500 m. Never re-record it.
3. Vessel model (ARCHITECTURE 7.2 and 3; fleet-docking 2.7): CraftRuntime, Vessel.crafts[], links[], helm { accountId, craft, controlPart }, PartRuntime.craft; nextStage, stageLockout, pending, sinceStaging and the abort sequence move to the craft; flow groups keyed (craft, stageGroup); crew, seats, hatch, cockpit id, the sensor-camera mount and the remote flag on the command part (the assembler copies VehicleDef.cockpit, .crew, .cameras.cockpit onto it); craft ids from an injected id source (a seeded counter locally); the id rules of ARCHITECTURE section 3 (craftId for a whole single craft, <craftId>~<root instance id> for a piece, a~<lowest id>~<tick> for anything of two or more craft, deterministic); part key craftId/instanceId everywhere outside the vessel; separateVessel computes components over tree edges AND links; pre-mated dock nodes become links. A momentum-conserving DOCK MERGE is ADDED (linear momentum of both, angular momentum about the new centre of mass including the orbital terms, w = I^-1 L; no tree is re-rooted). mergeVessels is NOT replaced: it is the weld of released clamp pieces into one held ground structure (they have no ports and would be split again by the component pass); keep it as a same-craft operation used only for that, covered by the guard. src/sim/vessel/public.ts keeps its signatures.
4. State is whole and versioned: friction anchors, thermal wake factors, wet flags and probe contact flags leave Vessel.struct and become vessel state. src/sim/vessel/codec.ts: binary, exact, non-finite numbers tagged, sign of zero preserved; a header with codec version and the defsHash it was written under; per craft a vehicle reference kind (library id plus content hash, or an embedded design) resolved through an INJECTED resolver, never defs.vehicles; per part the fingerprint of its PartDef; module and resource blocks length-prefixed so an unknown or changed block is detected. src/sim/vessel/migrations: a registry of pure functions from an old fingerprint's state to the new one (resource amounts clamped to capacity, mass properties recomputed), run on decode. encodeVessel/decodeVessel, a cheap copy for rollback rings, stateHash over codec output. Golden re-baseline 2 after the guard is green.
5. World speaks v2 (it stays the orchestrator until wave 4): SimSnapshot.frame with origin = the active vessel's SOI body and a rebase at SOI changes; a trivial time block; revision; crafts with stage info and chase-camera hints; per-part craftId, stageGroup and stageLabel; boundingRadius; the deprecated fields are still filled. src/session/index.ts exports createSession(defs, scenarioId, { terrain }) returning World typed as LocalSession; tests/mission and tools/sim import it; createSim in src/sim/index.ts stays as a deprecated alias (the lead removes it after the sweep).
6. Sites and loader: LaunchSiteDef.pads[] (PadDef of ARCHITECTURE 9.3) with the deprecated single pad still exposed as pads[0]; the site becomes ka-lae with pad lc-1 (files, scenarios, region file, start-time.json, tests in one commit); flatten discs derived from pads at load; ScenarioDef gains pad; an overlay DefSource (a second root whose bodies replace or add to the first, so staged bodies load without a $ref leaving a defs root); data/defs/rules/{default,staging,local}.json written from the contract defaults.

ACCEPTANCE (measured, in the hand-off):
- Step 1: the tolerance comparison table against baseline-v1 (every milestone); checkStartConstraints and the solstice test pass on the tick-aligned start; a unit test proves every scenario start and every rails landing is an integer tick.
- Trajectory guard bit-identical after steps 3, 4, 5 and 6 (attended craft, the six fixtures, the clamp vessel); debris within its fate tolerance; npm run test:mission passes with cheatCounter 0 and zero incomplete terrain queries; each re-baselined golden hash reproduces on a second run.
- Codec: encode/decode of a lander 60 and 150 steps into a touchdown, a capsule at peak heating, a stack mid-staging and a coasting vessel gives an equal state hash at load and a bit-identical continuation for 6,000 steps; sizes reported (target under 9 kB for the 38-part stack). A fixture written by codec version N-1 and one written under a changed PartDef (a module added, a tank resized) decode through the registry; an unknown block is reported, not mis-read; a design that is not in the library round-trips through the embedded kind.
- Merge then split of two craft restores every part pose to 1e-9 m and conserves linear momentum to 1e-6 and angular momentum to 1e-9 relative; a ring of three links splits correctly; two craft of the same vehicle in one vessel fire only their own stages; ids are unique and deterministic through dock, base-craft undock and re-dock.
- The terrain guard is green; npm run typecheck is clean for the whole tree (presentation compiles against the deprecated fields).
SELF-VERIFY: npm run typecheck; node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=cpu -- npx vitest run src/sim src/session src/core/defs src/terrain tests/unit/sim-vessel tests/unit/sim-world tests/unit/sim-orbits tests/unit/terrain-core tools/dev; node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=cpu -- npm run test:mission.

workPackages.title: Body definitions for the whole solar system, generated and validated against JPL Horizons
workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: docs/research/v2/solar-system.md (all; sources, tables, traps), ARCHITECTURE sections 8.1-8.3, src/core/contracts/defs.ts (the v2 BodyDef fields the lead has written), docs/handoff/lead-baseline-v2.md, docs/handoff/sim-orbits.md.

You produce DATA, staged so that nothing live changes: data/defs/bodies is not yours and stays untouched until the activation package (wave 4.4). You start after the lead's contract step, so the v2 BodyDef type exists; the loader's validation of the new fields and the overlay source are written by sim-core-v2 in parallel, so your own gate is the type and your tool's validation, and solar-system-sim loads your files through the loader as its first check in wave 4.

SCOPE (ARCHITECTURE 8.1-8.3): tools/bodies generates one BodyDef JSON per body into data/staged/bodies/ for exactly this list: Sun; Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune; Moon; Phobos, Deimos; Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto; Mimas, Enceladus, Tethys, Dione, Rhea, Titan, Iapetus; Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, Oberon; Triton; Ceres; Pluto, Charon (32 bodies). Source tables are kept in the tool with their URLs (JPL approximate positions Table 1 with rates and fitted mean motion; JPL satellite mean elements with plane frames ecliptic / parentEquator / explicit Laplace pole, the POSITIVE pole for Uranus; pck00011 poles, prime meridians, radii; body-only GM = system GM minus listed moons; SBDB elements for Ceres and Pluto). Earth: orbit { kind: sunLowPrecision, inverted: true }; Moon: its existing frozen ellipse unchanged. THE TOOL ALSO EMITS EACH NEW SOLID BODY'S TERRAIN SECTION (data/staged/terrain/<id>.terrain.json: tile set id = body id, resident level, amplification model key rocky-generic or icy-generic by body class with parameters from the body's data; planet-bake defines those models), referenced by a $ref that is relative to the root the file lives in, so the same path works under data/staged (through the overlay DefSource) and under data/defs after activation; no $ref ever leaves a root (the loader rejects that). Earth and the Moon reference their existing sections. Render data this wave is the inline impostor data only (mean colour, geometric albedo); planet-render adds the render section refs (atmospheres, cloud tops, rings, surface materials) in wave 5. Shape (equatorial/polar radius) for the oblate bodies, surface none plus atmosphere floor for the four giants, Saturn's ring block, physics atmospheres (exponential for Mars and the giants; table for Venus and Titan from public references you fetch and cite), heating sets per gas, soiRadius auto, mean colour and geometric albedo. The Sun is the root attractor with emission. Never transcribe by hand what the tool can compute.
VALIDATION: tools/bodies/validate fetches JPL Horizons state vectors (ICRF, parent-centred; cache under data/cache/bodies, use a generic client name) at ten epochs over 2030-2060 and fails when a planet exceeds the JPL table's stated accuracy or a moon exceeds 1 degree of phase or 2 % of radius. workPackages.title: Tile packs, the boot pack and their delivery; CI and the image; the local stack (one command, no cloud resource); the stage-0 skeleton on Railway's Hobby plan; first cloud measurements
workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: docs/research/v2/hosting-small.md (all: the Hobby plan's limits and prices, stage 0, the idle state, the local stack and what was measured for it; where it differs from ARCHITECTURE on the idle level, the two buckets, the egress budgets, the mirror's slices and the workspace bill, ARCHITECTURE is the later document and wins; and its section 9, the list of what you measure), docs/research/v2/hosting.md, docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS_V2.md (Answered, Q2, Q5, Small things and "Outside the three providers": what is approved and the pass/fail thresholds), ARCHITECTURE sections 6.2 (the idle state), 10.2, 10.4, 10.5, 13.1, 15.2 (cluster settings), 15.3 (the dump), 16 (all four parts), 27, 29.2, 30, docs/handoff/terrain-core.md, docs/handoff/bake-earth.md, docs/handoff/lead-baseline-v2.md, tools/server/dataPlugin.ts, src/terrain/provider.ts.

PROVIDED BY THE LEAD: the S3 client and presigner dependencies; embedded-postgres (PostgreSQL 18) and pg with its types; the npm script stack (it runs your deploy/local/stack.mjs); TileSourceSpec in terrain.ts; .gitignore entries (data/packs, data/stack); the heavy-job class stack (one slot, held by your launcher for as long as a stack is up); the Docker VM memory cap in .wslconfig; a CI-only build script; npm run stack:client (the production client build for the stack, written under data/stack/client, never to dist/: your shell role serves it with --page=build); the dev server serving /endpoints.json from the file named by STACK_ENDPOINTS, and a globalSetup that uses STACK_URL when it is set. The user has approved the Railway project fable-space-program and the Modal environment fsp (OPEN_QUESTIONS, Answered): you create both, on the HOBBY plan, and nothing that needs Pro. You define TilePackIndex in src/terrain/packIndex.ts (the lead lifts it into the contract afterwards). You do NOT touch the tile workers (src/render/terrain): presentation-sweep makes them take a TileSourceSpec after you.

SCOPE A - packs (ARCHITECTURE 10.4): tools/pack reads a baked tile set and writes content-addressed packs of 64-256 MB to data/packs/<tileset>/ plus an index (per tile group: pack, offset, length): all layers of one tile coordinate adjacent, groups in Morton order per level, height layers in separate packs, a small body as one pack per layer. Tile bytes are copied unchanged. data/packs is at most 20 GB and is NOT deleted after the first upload: it is kept until a copy outside the production bucket exists (the Modal volume filled through the presigned pack list; ARCHITECTURE 10.4) and the lead says so. src/terrain/tileSource.ts exports createTileSource(spec: TileSourceSpec) for the kinds fs, fetch (delegating to the existing sources, unchanged) and pack; src/terrain/packSource.ts is the ranged-HTTP source (coalesces neighbouring groups into one range; an ordered mirror list with failover on 429, 5xx, a timeout, 404 for an object the index promises, and 403 after ONE refresh of the pack list (an expired signature); it checks the status and the body length against the offset and length it knows from the index and NEVER depends on reading Content-Range, which is not a CORS-safelisted response header; a mirror mode taken from the pack list, either ranges of /p/<hash> or fixed aligned slice objects /p/<hash>/<n> whose size the pack list states (2 MB by default; the mode and the size are chosen by your measurement D5 and are never compiled in); works in the main thread, in workers and in Node); src/terrain/opfsCache.ts caches by content hash so a changed URL never causes a re-download. THE BOOT PACK: one small content-addressed pack holding the baked data the title needs (levels 0-3 of Earth and Moon, low mips of the sky and cloud maps, menu assets), budget 25 MB including the bundle and the definition library, which are built from the repository and are NOT in the pack; sky data and public/assets take the pack path. HOW IT REACHES SHELL (ARCHITECTURE 10.4): data/tiles is git-ignored, so neither CI nor Railway's build has baked data and the boot pack can never be built into the image; tools/pack uploads it to the packs bucket under its content hash and writes the tracked manifest deploy/boot-manifest.json (hash, bytes, what is deferred); the shell role fetches it once at start with the packs credential, verifies the hash, serves it from memory at the immutable URL /boot/<hash>.pack and passes its health check only when it is loaded; shell reports the boot manifest hash and the client build hash, which the rollout checks against the release commit. No Git LFS and no un-ignored upload.
SCOPE B - buckets and mirrors: TWO buckets (ARCHITECTURE 10.4: a Railway bucket credential cannot be read-only or scoped to a prefix): packs (the packs and the boot pack; its credential goes to game, to shell and to your upload tool) and dumps (database dumps and audit journals; its credential goes ONLY to the dump role and, as a Modal secret, to fsp-offsite and fsp-audit); scripts under deploy/ that upload packs to the packs bucket (S3 API), set CORS for ranged GET from a cross-origin-isolated page, and produce a presigned pack list signed with the date quantised to the UTC day and a lifetime of 7 days (the presigner's maximum: one URL for every client for a day, good for at least six more days); no code path of any role deletes or overwrites a pack. THE PROGRAM ENTRY AND THE ROLE MANIFEST (ARCHITECTURE 16.1): one Node program that starts the roles ROLES names, each from the entry the manifest gives, and hands each the shared services (the logger, the egress meter); server-persistence adds the game roles to the manifest in wave 5, and server/ never imports deploy/. The static roles as small servers under deploy/roles and Railway service definitions under deploy/, all started from the ONE image definition: shell (static, COOP/COEP headers, the client build as immutable hashed assets, index.html and /endpoints.json sent no-cache so the CDN does not hold them for its default two hours, the boot pack loaded from the bucket as above; CDN on; autodeploy on its own watch paths), packs (a streaming proxy of the packs bucket with immutable cache headers, in range or slice mode; AT STAGE 0 IT RUNS INSIDE THE SHELL SERVICE behind the shell's CDN, streaming without a disk cache inside a 0.5 vCPU / 0.25 GB replica limit, so tile traffic never touches the process that runs the universe; a service of its own with replicas and a disk cache only at stage 3) and dump (ROLES=dump, run as a cron service: the image installs the PGDG postgresql-client-18 beside Node, so pg_dump is of the server's major, and the role refuses to run otherwise; pg_dump -Fc to the dumps bucket, skipped when meta.change_seq has not moved since the last dump, retention of 24 hourly, 14 daily and 8 weekly copies pruned by the job itself, an upload budget of 1.5 GB a day that lengthens the interval; ONE Dockerfile, no second image; server-persistence gives the dump its real schema in wave 5). THE ENDPOINT DOCUMENT (ARCHITECTURE 13.1): shell serves GET /endpoints.json from its configuration: { v, build, gate[], api[], pub[], bootPack { url, hash, bytes } }, each list ordered candidates; it is the only way a client finds the servers, and the stage scripts change it by redeploying shell. THE EGRESS BUDGETS OF SHELL (ARCHITECTURE 16.2), counted in process per route and reset at 00:00 UTC, every one a setting: the client build 3 GB a day (then 503 with Retry-After for misses of hashed assets), the boot pack 1 GB a day (then a redirect to the presigned copy in the bucket), the mirror 8 GB a day (then 429, so clients stay on the bucket); every hashed route (/p/, /boot/, the assets) answers 404 with no body to a request that has a query string (Railway's CDN keys on the full query string, so cache-busting would make every request a billed miss); origin bytes limited per client address (300 MB in 10 minutes on the mirror); the egress meter is one small module under deploy/roles that the program entry also hands to the server roles. YOU DO NOT WRITE THE PUBLISHER: pub has ONE implementation, in server/ (server-persistence, wave 5), which also runs as ROLES=pub when it becomes a service; in this wave a hello role stands where each server role will be. No Netlify file is shipped (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q3).
SCOPE C - repository pipeline, image and the local stack: GitHub Actions for the secrets check, the stub scan, typecheck (both configurations), boundaries, unit suites on synthetic terrain (CI has no tiles and no GPU), the production client build and the server image, built on every push and smoke-tested; a buildId (a hash of the Node image digest and the server bundle hash) computed in the build, printed by every role at start and recorded by CI (at stage 0 Railway builds the same Dockerfile from the repository because the Hobby plan cannot pull a private registry image, so the buildId is what proves the two builds are one; the push to the registry by digest is written but used only from stage 1); path filters and a time budget of 8 minutes per push (private repository: Actions minutes are finite; report minutes per run). A Dockerfile with the Node version pinned by digest (journal replay depends on it). THE LOCAL STACK (ARCHITECTURE 16.4; hosting-small section 8 is its measured basis): deploy/local/stack.mjs behind npm run stack starts, with NO Docker and no cloud resource, a real PostgreSQL 18 from embedded-postgres in data/stack/<name>/pg, CREATED WITH PRODUCTION'S CLUSTER SETTINGS through initdbFlags ['--encoding=UTF8', '--locale-provider=builtin', '--builtin-locale=C.UTF-8'] (the package's default on this machine is a WIN1252 cluster with a Windows collation: text outside that code page fails to insert, citext follows another collation than production, a production dump may not restore; the stack refuses to start on a data directory whose server_encoding or datlocprovider differs) and stopped with the bundled pg_ctl stop -m fast, never with the package's own stop(), which is a hard kill on Windows; the role processes named in the role manifest as host Node processes in a NAMED SHAPE: --shape=combined (the default: game and shell), split (gate, dir carrying api and pub, sim-1, sim-2, shell, over TCP: the stage-2 wiring) or launch (two gate processes, dir, sim-1, sim-2, api, pub, shell and packs, each its own process: the stage-3 wiring); in this wave the manifest holds your static roles and a hello role per server role, and server-persistence adds the game roles in wave 5 without changing the launcher; the page source: --page=dev (the default: the existing dev server, which also serves the plain-file tiles, started with STACK_ENDPOINTS) or --page=build (your shell role serving the lead's stack:client build and the boot pack; the launcher runs npm run stack:client first); a small HTTP server over data/packs that behaves like the bucket (ranged GET with CORS, presigned-style URLs whose expiry it honours, switches that answer 403, 404 or 429 for the failover tests) and like the mirror in both of its modes; the stack's own endpoint document, written to data/stack/<name>/endpoints.json and served, which is the ONLY way a client is told an address; options --rules, --fresh, --shape, --page, --profile=acceptance|load (the load profile has its own memory bound, servers 4 GB and clients 2 GB, and does not start with less than 16 GB of physical memory free), --db=docker, --compose, and the variable STACK_NAME (one port range, because only one stack runs at a time; the name separates the data directories of runs that follow each other). THERE IS NO BACKGROUND MODE (ARCHITECTURE 16.4): heavy.mjs frees a slot when the wrapped command exits, so the launcher IS the wrapped command and lives as long as the stack: npm run stack -- [options] -- <command> brings the stack up, runs the command with STACK_URL, STACK_ENDPOINTS and STACK_STATE set, and brings the stack down when it exits, whatever its exit code, and on a signal; without a command it stays in the foreground until it is interrupted; status (from another terminal: what runs, with resident memory) and down (cleans up after a launcher that died: no process, no open port, the slot free). deploy/local/compose.yml, the high-fidelity form for the suites that need it: the pinned role image, the Postgres 18 image Railway's template is built on, MinIO as the S3 store; packs bind-mounted or tiles served over HTTP from a host process, NEVER the plain-file tree through a bind mount (36 times slower, measured); reached through the same launcher with --compose, in the same slot, which starts the Docker daemon if it is stopped and stops what it started; POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS in the compose file carries the same cluster settings; every later package uses both forms with its own STACK_NAME (document the variables). deploy/README.md with exact commands and the variable names each service needs.
SCOPE D - the stage-0 skeleton on Railway and the first measurements. Create the Railway project fable-space-program (environment production) in the shape of stage 0 of ARCHITECTURE 16.2, on the HOBBY plan: game (a hello role built by Railway from the repository with the Dockerfile; autodeploy off; health check that passes in standby; RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS=45; restart policy Always; replica limit 2 vCPU / 2 GB), shell (your static and packs roles with their egress budgets and the endpoint document, CDN on, limit 0.5 vCPU / 0.25 GB), postgres (the template on the Postgres 18 image; POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--encoding=UTF8 --locale-provider=builtin --builtin-locale=C.UTF-8 SET BEFORE ITS FIRST BOOT, because encoding and locale provider are fixed at creation like the major version; shared_buffers=96MB, max_wal_size=256MB, min_wal_size=64MB, max_connections=40 through ALTER SYSTEM; limit 1 vCPU / 0.5 GB, which is what bounds its billed page cache at $5 a month; 5 GB volume), dump (an hourly cron service running the dump role of the SAME image, holding the dumps credential), TWO buckets in US East, packs with the packs and the boot pack uploaded and dumps; and the Modal environment fsp with the dumps credential as a secret and a volume that receives a copy of the packs (copied on Modal through the presigned pack list). No hard usage limit (Railway's is per workspace and would stop the other project); no Serverless; no alert. If the Railway GitHub App has no access to the repository yet (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q5), deploy by uploading a clean export of the tagged tree with the logged-in CLI and say so. Then measure (hosting-small section 9): (1) billed memory and CPU of the idle skeleton per service over at least 6 hours and AGAIN after at least 72 hours of uptime with dump runs in the window (page cache creeps until the replica limit pushes back), from Railway's usage figures per service and per project (railway usage --json, railway usage projects), projected to a month by the formula of ARCHITECTURE 29.2 against the estimate and the $30 ceiling; the workspace's usage and estimated bill at the time (already read on 2026-11-10: the other project uses the included $5, $7.40 estimated for the period and $10.23 for the one before, so the game's usage is billed in full); (2) which Postgres major the template created, whether POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS took effect (server_encoding UTF8, the built-in locale provider) and whether ALTER SYSTEM was accepted; (3) the deploy overlap of game on Hobby: standby health check, when SIGTERM arrives, whether the 45 s drain is honoured, where new connections go during the overlap, the build time from the repository and whether Hobby builds were paused; (4) a Postgres restart under a connected hello role: time to reconnect; (5) from Chrome under COEP against the deployed services: ranged GET of a presigned bucket URL with CORS (and, for the record, whether the bucket honours ExposeHeaders: nothing depends on it); WHAT THE CDN DOES WITH Range (Railway announced support in July 2026): is a ranged response cached, and does a ranged miss pull only that range from the origin or the whole object; from that, THE MIRROR'S MODE (ranges if both hold, otherwise slices of 2 MB, or 1 MB) and, in that mode, first-byte time cold and warm, hit rate from the origin's logs, billed egress per GB delivered, BYTES SENT PER BYTE NEEDED over the recorded first session of (8) (pass: at most 1.5, otherwise the slice size goes down) and the time to the first decoded tile beside the bucket path's; that a request with a query string gets a 404 and no bytes; whether the origin sees the client's address behind the CDN (for the per-address limit); failover between the two, including an expired URL (403, one refresh of the pack list, then failover) and a 404; the boot pack's redirect to the bucket once its budget is spent; cold first-byte time of the boot pack from the shell against the bucket; (6) bucket throughput: a Modal fleet (app fsp-probe; expressed as concurrent fetchers per container, at most 40 containers) at 20, 500 and 2,000 concurrent fetchers replaying real tile range requests for 15 minutes against the presigned packs, judged against the pass/fail numbers of ARCHITECTURE 10.4 (bucket egress is free, so this costs nothing on Railway; the mirror at launch size is NOT tested here: it belongs to the launch rehearsal); (7) the cloud derating: the real stepVessel regimes of codebase-audit 3.3 with 1, 2, 4 and 8 SYNCHRONISED workers stepping the same tick on the game replica with its limit raised to 8 vCPU / 8 GB for the run and put back afterwards (sleep-scheduled, not spinning), p50/p99 per thread at each count, billed vCPU-seconds per vessel-second and idle CPU, against the same benchmark on the development machine (16 and 22 workers need a Pro replica and belong to the launch rehearsal); (8) the bytes and requests of a recorded first session (boot, calibration data, title, one launch to orbit), on the bucket path and AS BYTES ACTUALLY TRANSFERRED in the mirror's mode, with which the 300 MB per visitor, 15 TB and $750 figures of ARCHITECTURE 30, the per-visitor and worst-case figures of 10.4 and the mirror's daily budget are recomputed. Total Railway spend of this scope: under $5; print it. Leave the skeleton running at its idle floor: it is the production environment that deploy-loadtest fills in wave 6. If a platform fault stops the deployment, deliver A-C, every measurement script with a dry run against the local stack, and say plainly which numbers are still unmeasured.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Every tile read through createTileSource({kind:'pack'}) is byte-identical to the fs source for the earth and moon tile sets (full sweep in a test), in whole-pack mode and in both mirror modes (ranges and slices); small-body tile sets are swept when they exist (the test iterates the tile sets present); request count for a recorded 10-minute flight trace is at least 5 times lower than per-file fetching.
- tests/browser/platform: a page reads tiles through the pack source on the main thread and in a worker against the local stack (CORS, COEP, no dependence on Content-Range), hits the OPFS cache on reload, and fails over to the second mirror when the first returns 429, when it returns 404 for an indexed object, and after one refresh of the pack list when it returns 403 for an expired URL; a terrain hash at fixed points computed through the pack source equals the terrain guard.
- The boot set (the first-paint chunks of the client build plus the boot pack) is at most 25 MB; a cold load of it over a 50 Mbit/s throttle against the local stack with --page=build (your shell serving the lead's stack:client build and the boot pack it loaded from the bucket stand-in) completes in under 8 s (the title itself is assembled later by app-integration-1); shell does not pass its health check with a missing pack or a wrong hash; deploy/boot-manifest.json matches the uploaded object.
- EGRESS BUDGETS (unit tests and against the local stack): each shell route stops sending at its budget and answers as specified (503, the redirect, 429); a query string on /p/, /boot/ or a hashed asset gets a 404 with no body; the per-address limit holds; the counters reset at 00:00 UTC; /endpoints.json is served no-cache and lists its candidates in order.
- CI runs green on a branch in under 8 minutes, builds the client and the image, and fails on a planted secret, a planted TODO and a boundary violation.
- THE LOCAL STACK: npm run stack starts from nothing with the Docker daemon stopped and no network; Postgres is ready in under 1 s after its first initialisation; two sessions contend for one advisory lock and exactly one gets it; a fenced write with a stale token changes 0 rows; a committed row survives a hard kill of Postgres and of the launcher; the cluster is UTF8 with the built-in C.UTF-8 locale, a text with characters outside Windows-1252 round-trips, citext uniqueness is case-insensitive, and the stack refuses a data directory created otherwise; --shape=split and --shape=launch start their processes on their own ports; status reports resident memory at or under 0.6 GB for this wave's stack (Postgres, the static roles, the tile servers); THE SLOT: while a stack is up heavy.mjs --status shows the stack slot held by the launcher, a second npm run stack waits and does not start a second stack, the slot is free the moment the wrapped command has exited and the stack is down, and after the launcher is killed down leaves no process and no open port and the slot is reclaimed (each checked by a test); two runs with different STACK_NAME values, one after the other, leave separate data directories and share no state. The compose form starts with the VM capped at 6 GB, serves the same pack requests, its Postgres has the same encoding and locale provider, and the dump role in the pinned image dumps it and pg_restore restores the dump, also into the host stack's embedded cluster; the image smoke test runs a role in the pinned image and prints the same buildId as CI.
- THE STAGE-0 SKELETON is deployed on the Hobby plan and reachable: the shell serves the boot pack it loaded from the packs bucket, with the isolation headers, through the CDN, and serves the endpoint document; the hello game answers its health check in standby and survives a redeploy with the drain honoured; the dump job has written and pruned dumps in the dumps bucket, and neither game nor shell holds that bucket's credential; the database reports UTF8 and the built-in locale provider; nothing that needs Pro was used. COST, MEASURED BY THE ONE FORMULA OF ARCHITECTURE 29.2: U is the skeleton's own usage for the window from Railway's per-project figures, projected to 730 hours; it is reported per service against the estimate, at 6 hours and again at 72; U + $5 is at or under $30; the workspace's bill, max($5, U plus the other project's usage), is printed beside it. If the ceiling is missed, that is the first line of the report, with the line that caused it.
- docs/capacity/<date>-platform.md reports, for every measurement that ran: idle usage in dollars per service and its monthly projection; billed memory of game and Postgres idle, at 6 and at 72 hours; the workspace's usage beside the skeleton's; the Postgres major, encoding and locale provider and the ALTER SYSTEM result; the overlap, drain and build timings; p50/p95 first byte, error rate and aggregate throughput of the bucket at each concurrency against the pass/fail numbers; what the CDN does with Range and the mirror mode chosen; the mirror path's CDN hit rate, billed egress per GB and bytes sent per byte needed; cold first byte of the boot pack from the shell and from the bucket; per-thread step time at 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers and the derating that follows; the first-session bytes with the recomputed per-visitor and worst-case figures; the cost of the tests. Numbers, not adjectives. If the bucket fails at 500 or 2,000 fetchers, say so on the first line: stage 0 is unaffected, and the escalation of OPEN_QUESTIONS is the lead's to raise before any launch is announced.
- No existing Modal app or volume and no existing Railway project is touched (list what was created).
SELF-VERIFY: npx vitest run tests/unit/platform src/terrain/tileSource.test.ts src/terrain/packSource.test.ts; STACK_NAME=fsp-platform-delivery npm run stack -- -- <the pack sweep>; npm run stack -- --page=build -- node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=gpu -- npx playwright test tests/browser/platform --project=functional (the launcher holds the stack slot and stops the stack when the command exits); npm run stack -- --compose -- <the dump, restore and image smoke tests>.

RULES (docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, binding): (1) Edit only your owned paths; an entry starting with '!' is excluded. A change you need elsewhere is a request file in docs/requests/. The lead owns src/core/contracts (except the parts a brief names), the root configuration (package.json, the lockfile, tsconfig*.json, vite.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, playwright.config.ts, .gitignore), tools/dev, src/core/math, src/core/testing, labs/template and tests/browser/{harness,globalSetup,chromeArgs}.ts. Never run npm install: the dependencies and configuration entries you need are listed under PROVIDED BY THE LEAD in your brief, or are a request. (2) No placeholders, stubs, TODOs or silent fallbacks (CI scans for them); what cannot be finished is stated in the hand-off. (3) Engine code never names a specific body, vehicle, part, site, scenario or rule value; every number of the time model, pads, docking, expiry and rate limits is a UniverseRules field. (4) Headless code (src/sim, src/universe, src/session, src/terrain, src/pilot) uses no DOM, WebGPU, timers, Date, performance, Math.random, sockets or storage; npx vitest run tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts stays green. (5) Shared tree: verify with scoped commands only (npm run typecheck:paths -- <paths>; npx vitest run <paths>; npx playwright test <dir>); never npm run build or npm run check; every heavy command through node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=<cpu|gpu|bake|stack> -- <command>, one at a time; the only client build you may run is npm run stack:client (the lead's; it writes under data/stack, never to dist/); THE LOCAL STACK (host Node processes and an embedded Postgres 18, no Docker; ARCHITECTURE 16.4) NEVER RUNS IN THE BACKGROUND: start it only as npm run stack -- [options] -- <your suite command> with STACK_NAME=fsp-<package id> (the script takes the ONE stack slot of heavy.mjs, brings the stack up, runs your command with STACK_URL and STACK_ENDPOINTS set, and stops the stack when the command exits; a command inside it that needs the GPU is itself wrapped in heavy.mjs --class=gpu); hold the slot for one suite at a time and release it between suites, because other packages wait for it; the docker compose form (the pinned Linux image) is the same command with --compose, in the same slot, only for the suites your brief names, and it stops what it started, a Docker daemon included; never leave a server, database, browser or container running. (6) Git: only git add <your paths>, then commit; never add -A, stash, reset, rebase, amend or push (releases are tags the lead moves); commit working states often. (7) Write files with the Write tool, absolute paths. (8) Secrets (.env, provider tokens) are read only at run time by tools under tools/, server/, bots/ or deploy/; never printed, committed, logged in a URL or shipped to the client; run node tools/dev/check-secrets.mjs before every commit if you touch them. (9) Cloud: never touch existing Modal apps or volumes or the existing Railway project; create cloud resources only when your brief names them, only in the Railway project fable-space-program and the Modal environment fsp (both approved by the user: docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS_V2.md, Answered), on the Railway HOBBY plan and inside the stage-0 limits of ARCHITECTURE 16.2; anything that needs the Pro plan, raises the standing spend or is a rehearsal beyond what the Hobby plan allows is the lead's to announce to the user first: stop and ask the lead. Never build alert routing and never ask for a webhook. Everything else is built and verified on the local stack, which needs no cloud resource; never report a local-stack result as a deployed or measured-capacity result. (10) Browser work: real Chrome, real GPU, assert the adapter, close loops on state, LOOK at every screenshot you save; perf only under the GPU lock; where your brief names reference images, compare with the helper in tests/browser/harness.ts and never re-record one yourself. (11) Disk: data/ stays under 22 GB, data/packs under 20 GB, at least 25 GB of the disk free; delete intermediates. (12) Finish with docs/handoff/<package id>.md: public API with exact signatures, how to run and verify, measured numbers against every acceptance criterion (say plainly which were not met and why), known limits, and every contract change you request.

The Docker VM cap (.wslconfig) is the USER's to write, not yours and not the lead's: do not start Docker until the user has written it. The node rule of tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts allows Node builtins in src/terrain only in fs*.ts modules, and no Node networking or threads anywhere outside server/ and bots/.

workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: docs/research/v2/codebase-audit.md (all), docs/research/v2/frontend-ux.md section 10, MIGRATION_V2 sections 3 (step 3.11), 4 and 7, ARCHITECTURE sections 2 (import rules), 3 (frames, rebase), 17, 18.7, 18.8, 20, 31.3, docs/handoff/lead-baseline-v2.md (the deprecated fields; the reference images), docs/handoff/sim-core-v2.md, docs/handoff/platform-delivery.md (createTileSource), every wave-2 presentation hand-off.

YOU ARE ALONE IN THE PRESENTATION CODE THIS SUB-WAVE. sim-core-v2 has finished: World fills the new snapshot fields beside the deprecated ones and createSession exists. You move every consumer to the new fields, once, compiler-driven, one commit per subsystem; when your grep is clean the lead removes the deprecated fields. The gate for pixels is the REFERENCE IMAGES recorded by the lead.

SCOPE:
1. Snapshot consumers: SimSnapshot.tick -> revision; activeVesselId nullable with the neutral singleton blocks; part keys craftId/instanceId (vesselFeature keys state by rootOf(vessel.id) + instanceId today: two craft of one type collide); cockpit interior, seat and engine clusters from the command part and the part list; Readouts.target replaces targetBodyId/targetClosestApproach; the pause action becomes flightMenu; LaunchSiteDef.pads (siteFeature iterates pads).
2. RULE: presentation never indexes defs.vehicles by a runtime id. Known sites beyond the cockpit ones: src/ui/model.ts describeResources maps instanceId to a stage group through the vehicle definition (two docked craft of one type merge their bars; another vehicle's parts fall into a catch-all), and src/camera/chaseRig.ts takes its distance limits from the base craft's vehicle. Use PartSnapshot.stageGroup and stageLabel, VesselSnapshot.boundingRadius and CraftSnapshot camera hints.
3. Frame rebase: the lead's src/core/math/frame.ts applied by the render core's previous-frame state, the camera rigs, the map focus and world-anchored effects (vfx); presentation must be origin-agnostic (World now reports Moon-centred ROOT positions in lunar orbit).
4. FakeSim becomes FakeSession (src/core/fakes): the eight v1 scenes plus rendezvous (two craft, target readout), docking approach (docking readout, port states), assembly (three craft, links, helm), echoes (recorded and projected, time offsets) and a time-strip scene for each TimeView relation. A conformance test per scene that exists in the real session today (tests/unit/fakes): the fake's snapshot has the same field presence, units, frames and value ranges as createSession's in the same situation.
5. The tile-source seam: WorkerInit (src/render/terrain/workerProtocol.ts) carries a TileSourceSpec, the tile worker and streamer call createTileSource(spec) (today tileWorker.ts hard-codes createFetchTileSource(msg.tilesUrl)); the dev default stays fetch.
6. Render core additions that the menu and the settings packages build on next wave: the UI scrim step in the tonemap pass sampling the bloom pyramid inside 'ui.scrimRects' (no rectangles: no cost), CameraState.exposureHint { targetEv100, rateEvPerS } and lensShift honoured by the core. Document them in docs/RENDER_API.md.
7. src/app, index.html, labs/integration and every spec and lab move from createSim to createSession (src/session); specs that assert an Earth-centred rRoot are rewritten to differences.

ACCEPTANCE:
- npm run typecheck is clean for the whole tree; a grep test (tests/unit/fakes/deprecated.test.ts) proves no file outside src/sim and the loader reads a deprecated field or indexes defs.vehicles[ by a runtime id, and no presentation file assumes a ROOT origin at Earth.
- Every wave-2 unit and lab spec passes; EVERY reference image compares within its tolerance (the pad scenes may differ only by the one-pad-to-pad-list change; any other difference is a defect or a lead-signed re-record); the summed GPU budget table is unchanged within 3 % (perf project).
- A test renders the same frame with the frame origin at Earth and at the Moon and the images differ by less than 1/255 per channel; a rebase at an SOI change produces no visible step in a screenshot pair and no motion-vector spike.
- Two craft of the same vehicle in one vessel: resource bars, wear, staging and plume state never mix (unit tests on keys); the chase rig frames a three-craft assembly from its bounding radius.
- The terrain lab streams through a TileSourceSpec of kind fetch and of kind pack (against the local stack) with identical frames.
- Scrim step at most 0.1 ms GPU with four rectangles and unmeasurable with none; the browser mission's first minutes (pad to max-q) run in the integrated app on createSession.

Structural operations (split, destroy, add, remove, rebase, replace) as data with a result checksum, wrapping split.ts and staging.ts, applied identically by anyone who holds the island state. Threshold-watch flag. Nothing reaches the island except tick-stamped inputs (controls, commands, admissions, reservation results, adds and removes, range-safety and safing actions, helm grants, timer-derived inputs, rate changes); it reads no clock.

The island codec (src/sim/island/codec.ts; ARCHITECTURE 7.2): members with tier flags and the anchor, the reference orbit, nascent pairs, U5 pairs with their clearing timers, capture constraints and their timers (slots defined now, filled by contact-docking), threshold-watch flags, admitted copies with old heads and reservation state, a pending merge tick, per pilot the latched controls, open latch and dead-man timers and queued inputs; versioned like the vessel codec; islandHash over its output.
D. View (src/sim/view): pure builders from island state plus planning state: SimSnapshot with presentation interpolation, frame and rebase, readouts (target readouts through the navigation signatures), navball, staging info per craft, patches and markers, nodes and burn bookkeeping, surface targets from every site, TimeView from a clock description; full part snapshots only for vessels inside a relevance cut passed in, pose-only for the rest. PROVIDED BY THE LEAD: ws and its types, fflate; the presentation types of net.ts (UniverseRules, ClockState, TimeView, CensusEntry, TargetRef, view models). YOU WRITE AND OWN the wire-message section of src/core/contracts/net.ts (every message of ARCHITECTURE 13.3 as a typed union, InputAck, RelevantFull/RelevantDelta, the census documents) for the rest of the project; universe-directory, netcode-client and server-persistence file requests against it. The island codec (src/sim/island) is written by island-core in parallel: IslandEnter carries its output as an opaque, length-prefixed blob.

SCOPE: src/net imports src/core only and runs unchanged in Chrome, in Node and in a worker.
- THE SESSION LAYER, once, for both ends (this is what stops the client and the server from each writing their own against a mock): pure state machines with no I/O for Hello/Challenge/Auth/Welcome, resume and takenOver, version and defsHash mismatch, subscriptions (the relevant-set parameters, pads, roster, worldline), the per-client downstream budget and drop-superseded, the gateway's 5 s input buffer with acknowledged ticks, declared socket loss (1 s ping, 3 s without a frame), backoff. Each has a client half and a server half driven by the same recorded transcripts (tests/unit/net/transcripts), which netcode-client and server-persistence replay in their own suites.
- codec: encode/decode for every message type of net.ts. Batch framing (varint count, then u8 type, varint length, payload), little-endian, ticks as float64 integers, session-local u32 handles with a handle table message. IslandKey exact (float64 offsets from the reference orbit, float32 attitude and rate); InputAck (seq ranges applied as stamped, one entry per late input with its applied tick); IslandDelta groups against the last key: POSE quantised (position 1/64 mm with a coarse flag, velocity um/s, smallest-three quaternion, urad/s), CONTROL, PART-FAST, and the exact contact form; IslandSlow round-robin; IslandOp with checksums; IslandEnter carrying vessel-codec blobs deflated by the application; relevant-set entries (forecast-chain patches with validity ticks, about 84 B per patch) with full and delta forms and sequence numbers; the public census documents (a snapshot and sequence-numbered deltas per sphere of influence, fetched over HTTP, identical for every viewer) with the same entry codec; clock, conjunction, command and view-model messages. A decoder never throws on malformed input: it returns a typed error, bounded work per message.
- transports behind one interface: browser WebSocket, Node ws, an in-process loopback, and a length-prefixed stream for role-to-role links. Back-pressure: bufferedAmount-aware send that drops superseded latest-wins frames and never drops reliable ones.
- time sync (minimum-round-trip filter) and the input-margin feedback loop as pure functions.
- injector: a wrapper for any transport and a stand-alone proxy process that add fixed delay, jitter, TCP-style stalls (nothing lost, everything late), bandwidth caps and disconnects, per direction, scriptable from tests.
- a per-client downstream budget scheduler (priority: own island, near tier, the relevant set; default 6 kB/s; the complete census never rides the socket).
- a recorder/replayer of message streams for fixtures (used by the UI packages and by bots).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Round trip: every message type on 1,000 seeded random instances and on fixtures recorded from FakeSession scenes decodes to equal values; keys are bit-exact; quantisation error of deltas is at most 16 um, 1 um/s, 5e-10 rad (tested).
- Sizes with framing, reported per message: single-owner key at most 110 B per vessel; shared delta at most 130 B for two vessels and 300 B for ten; a staging IslandOp under 100 B; a census entry at most 90 B.
- Encode at most 5 us and decode at most 5 us per vessel for a delta on this machine (benchmark through the gate); zero allocations per message in steady state for the high-rate types.
- Fuzz: 1,000,000 random and mutated byte strings never throw, never read out of bounds, never allocate above 1 MB.
- The same test file passes in Node (vitest) and in Chrome (tests/browser/net: a Playwright spec loading the bundle; that directory is yours).
- Session layer: every transcript drives the client half against the server half over the loopback transport and over the injector at 300 ms with stalls to the same final states; resume after a drop mid-handshake, mid-subscription and with inputs in flight; a takenOver session stops sending; malformed and out-of-order messages are refused with a typed reason.
- The injector reproduces a scripted profile (150 ms +/- 20 ms, 5 % stalls of 200 ms) within 5 ms, measured.

workPackages.title: The universe: directory, clocks and the time rules, reservations and claims, forecast chains and screening, pads, expiry, the scheduler interface, UniverseHost; LocalSession beside World
workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: ARCHITECTURE sections 5 (every rule; it is your specification, including the vocabulary of 5.1 and the membership and carry-limit rules of 5.2), 6.1, 6.2, 7.2, 7.3, 9.3, 9.4, 15.5, 26 (time-request limits), 28.2 (the suites you write), docs/research/v2/proposal-server-simulates.md sections 2, 3.3, 8, docs/research/v2/proposal-adaptive-balance.md sections 2, 3, 9, docs/handoff/island-core.md (the island API), docs/handoff/solar-system-sim.md, docs/handoff/fleet-data.md, docs/handoff/wire-protocol.md (the message types UniverseHost emits).

You build the rules of the shared universe as pure TypeScript (time, up-time and storage injected through universe.ts, which you write and own from now on) on top of island-core's finished island. You do NOT touch src/sim/world: World keeps flying the mission; you build LocalSession BESIDE it in src/session, and the session-switch package makes it the default and deletes World after you. You do not build executors: the scheduler interface and the acceptance-window rule are yours, the trailing-batch executor and its lane-equivalence and migration suites are server-persistence's.

SCOPE:
A. Directory: records, worldlines, tombstones and lineage (ids of ARCHITECTURE 3), holder and epoch, hand-over as an in-memory flip written ahead, the per-body passive index, about 0.5 kB per passive vessel.
B. Clocks (5.2): closed-form schedules on up-time with untilTick (events, lead cap, carry limit, chain end); kinds live, cohort, private, shared; sticky membership, bound members and guests, fork on leave, follow; the carry limit (minimum over craft whose owners have not explicitly accepted, anchored to the live clock); the live clock as a persisted up-time mapping with the resume window.
C. Rules U1-U19 and U8b exactly as written, every number from UniverseRules: the solid window with the minimum-over-owned-craft limit; admit, RESERVE (exclusive, epoch-fenced, in memory, granted before a copy leaves the Armed tier; an island never steps an unreserved copy into the contact margin; release on parting, dissolve or fence; the loser's offer by relation; sweep, safing, fate and attach respect the reservation; grant, denial and release are journaled island inputs) and commit (the commit path exists; first-touch detection needs contact and is finished by contact-docking); materialisation with the bounded U5 exemption (inhibits, separation acceleration, recovery after 30 s); rate rules and proposals with per-account limits; jump, hold, meet with the refusal alternative (latest clean tick) and the chained jump; U8b seating; advance for a visitor; departures without delay; fates and the pacing clock (debris stays passive and solid to its horizon; Reduced tier and unattended runs paced by their pacing clock and solid to its islands); U16 with its one table (declared loss, latch and dead-man timers on up-time entering the island as stamped inputs, the clock holding, the explicit leave closing the throttle); the three timer bases.
D. Forecast chains and screening (src/sim/orbit/conjunction): the directory alone extends a passive vessel's chain lazily up to the furthest tick a viewer, a screening or a horizon search needs (cap 16 patches), stored as forecast worldline segments and published with validity ticks; horizon search over the chain; screening of rails trajectories against the solid predicate over an interval (shell filter, minimum distance between conics, closest approach in time, in-phase jump search) with re-screen on commit that never shortens untilTick to a displayed tick.
E. Island lifecycle with holder and epoch: an attended vessel at 4x or below is always in an island (rails state); cruising only above 4x, materialised before controls are live; merge with a pending merge tick that neither island steps past; split; to rails; migrate by value (island codec); drain lag before any read; the vessel budget of 64 as a performance budget (no merge or admission refused; dilation, keep-out notice, deterministic fragment merging). The scheduler interface (the caller says how much up-time it has) and lagCap, tau and the acceptance window, with every input acknowledged with its applied tick.
F. 5. - Boot order: the inlined gate, then the shell state machine from the title on the boot set and the class-hint preset; deferred loading with real progress in the status line; the calibration side state at the first Play, started only when resident() says its data is in; the chosen QualityProfile applied through Renderer.setQuality; settings persisted per adapter fingerprint.
- The loop of ARCHITECTURE 17.2 with input contexts (menu, transit, flight), the camera rigs (menu, turntable, transit, chase, cockpit, map), the session's stores feeding the shell, the in-process PlanningService behind the map and the HUD (never a simulation import in src/map or src/ui), audio buses, the test API (sessionKind, stores()).
- Deploy flow on LocalSession: vehicle and pad selection, the transit with its gates, hand-over to flight, the flight menu and leaving, My Ships on the local universe, Practice (offline) as a first-class path, Credits.
- /?scenario=lunar-direct&pilot=1 keeps working for the browser mission.

You own all of src/sim, src/universe and src/session this wave, and src/core/defs for link and port validation, and answer the requests other packages file against them (site structure files belong to fleet-models-pads this wave; body render sections to planet-render). The reservation mechanism, the carry limit, forecast chains and the island codec exist (universe-directory, island-core): you make contact real on top of them. The geometric data of existing parts and src/sim/vessel/public.ts signatures stay frozen (the model team builds on them concurrently).

SCOPE:
- Colliders: clearance.ts becomes the collider library: default shapes from bounds, authored CollisionShapeDef shapes, a bounding-volume tree per vessel in VES, GJK distance with closest features and normal (exact for near-parallel faces), conservative advancement for time of impact.
- The island pair pass: sphere sweep per pair per step; speculative contacts for slow pairs; time of impact for fast pairs; sequential impulses (8 iterations, order by vessel id then part index, restitution 0.2 above 0.3 m/s, friction 0.5, positional correction) in the 480 Hz sub-steps with equal and opposite forces in the same sub-step. THE INTEGRATOR RULE (ARCHITECTURE 6.2, 7.4): free flight stays RK4 at 120 Hz; a pair enters the sub-stepped path when the sweep puts it inside the speculative-contact margin and leaves when it is outside again, both vessels at the same tick, through the hook island-core left; the born-overlapping rule (nascent pairs until 5 cm apart).
- Damage: contact, crash (energy share against crashTolerance, joints by the g rule, separateVessel) and hypervelocity (NASA breakup energy rule, 40 kJ/kg catastrophic) regimes; explosions reach other vessels; at most twelve new vessels per collision, and fragments beyond the island's vessel budget merged into the nearest surviving fragment or turned into effects, deterministically by id order (no merge or admission is ever refused: the budget is a performance budget); collision events with identical numbers for both parties; destructive outcomes between two owners raise the flush-now flag so the directory commits them at once, and carry provisional until durable.
- Docking: port state machine (disabled, ready, occupied, soft, hard, cooldown), capture envelope measured between port frames, soft capture as a compliant six-axis constraint in the pair pass, hard dock merge at a tick with momentum conserved, link strength, undock with the impulse at the port point, stage action undock; ops capture, release, merge, split. IDS AND LINEAGE at dock and undock exactly as ARCHITECTURE section 3 (an assembly id issued at the first dock; absorbed rows become tombstones that keep their worldlines; a craft that undocks alone reopens its own row; the piece with the most craft keeps the assembly id; targets, plans and census handles follow lineage). Two craft reaching one port in one step: the second receives captureLost { reason: occupied }. The island codec's constraint slots are filled (soft-capture constraint with its 0.5 s clamp and 60 s timers, the hard-dock dwell timer).
- Assemblies: helm; the anchor by seniority among craft with an unexpired owner, passing with its helm policy when its owner lapses or it leaves; a VACANT helm granted at once to a pilot aboard whom the policy admits, an OCCUPIED helm by request (grant, or 30 s of up-time without helm input); the helm seat reserved for the reconnect grace after a declared socket loss unless the anchor's owner takes it (the one table of U16); unowned-attached craft on the default lend policy with ports any owner may release; the advance limit of an assembly as the minimum over its owned craft and the carry limit on its clock; docked free drift and lend policies in the actuator allocation, craft sovereignty (ownership checked on every command), control-from-here, transfer and cross-feed (closed form on rails), assembly limits.
- Universe: first-touch commit for the reservation holder (unconditional; the island steps on, the event waits for the durable write), two-owner transitions through the commit-before-release path with the journal chunk up to the transition tick, armed-tier wake-up and the reservation request at the armed margin, the departure screening of U11, the jump screening of U8 and the U5 exemption with real radii (inhibits, separation acceleration, recovery), encounters integrated with swept tests, Reduced-tier debris and unattended runs admitted into islands of their pacing clock, range safety and pad keep-out recovery as journaled inputs, debris budgets.
- Navigation and readouts: Readouts.docking (port frames, per-limit flags, phase), SAS modes target, antiTarget, portAlign as attitude holds.
- Pilots (src/pilot/generic): rendezvous (plans with nodes against a target's chain, uses jump, meet and warp requests as a player would) and docking (target mode, port alignment, RCS translation), acting only through FlightSession.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Trajectory guard green with the pair pass on; npm run test:mission passes; every one of the ten stage separations of meridian-lunar and of each new vehicle leaves the pieces undamaged.
- Two craft closing at 0.1, 10, 300, 7,800 and 15,600 m/s, at 64 phases of the step and 16 lateral offsets: never pass through each other; the regime and the destroyed parts match the rule tables.
- Capture succeeds 1 % inside and fails 1 % outside each of the six envelope limits for both port types; a miss below crash tolerance bounces and names the limit.
- Dock then undock: part poses restored to 1e-9 m; linear momentum to 1e-6 and angular to 1e-9 relative through capture, merge and release; a side-port undock produces the computed turn; a ring of three is one vessel; a 1 MN burn through a C port breaks the link and a Pelican push does not.
- A dock at 30 AU from the Sun (island frame) reaches hard dock with relative speed noise under 1 mm/s.
- Two craft entering one port in one tick resolve identically live and in replay; a claim is committed only on first touch (fly-by at 500 m leaves the head and releases the reservation).
- TWO ISLANDS AT DIFFERENT TICKS touching one passive station in the same wall millisecond, at docking speed and as a 1 km/s impact: exactly one touches it; the other resolved no contact, capture or crash against it; identical in replay.
- A stage dropped by pad 1's rocket hits pad 2's rocket launched two minutes later (Reduced-tier debris on the live clock, admitted, swept, crash regime).
- The integrator boundary: two craft 20 m apart in low Earth orbit and at 30 AU crossing the speculative-contact margin in both directions gain under 0.1 mm/s of relative velocity; a hard dock still meets its 3 mm/s threshold.
- Island codec: checkpoint, restore and continue in the middle of a soft capture and with a nascent pair: bit-identical. A 65th vessel approaching an island at its budget still collides.
- Ids: dock, undock of the base craft alone, re-dock, a break into three: unique at every tick, no reuse while live, echoes intact for a viewer behind each operation.
- Helm: a ferry docking to an empty station gets the helm at once; a helm whose socket is lost keeps its seat for the grace; the carry-limit cases with a real dock (vacant helm of a docked parked ship warps only to that ship's limit).
- THE REFUELLED PROFILE, flown on LocalSession by the pilots: the cruiser raises itself, docks with a depot, takes propellant through the port, and departs to a body beyond its unrefuelled reach, ending in a bound orbit there.
- The remaining adversarial cases of ARCHITECTURE 28.2 pass (station-keeping neighbour, ram inside 30 s, SOI crossing during a merge).
- The docking pilot docks a solstice-kestrel to a parked solstice-atoll on LocalSession in under 40 minutes of flight time from a co-orbit 5 km behind, 20 seeded starts, at least 19 successes; the rendezvous pilot reaches the station from a pad launch in a window slot.
- Cost: pair pass for two 40-part craft at arm's length at most 0.1 ms per step; a parked station armed beside an approaching ferry costs under 1 us per second until 200 m.
