LEAD NOTE (2026-11-12, after the independent review of sim-core-v2; it overrides the brief above where they differ): CRAFT IDENTITY (ARCHITECTURE 3, 7.2, 7.5; built by sim-core-v2, vessel codec version 3). Craft ids are universe-unique: at no tick do two craft carry the same id, in one vessel or in two. A craft has one part tree with one root part. At assembly every part tree that a dock link joins to another is its own craft (a vehicle with pre-mated ports is an assembly of several craft from its first tick). At a separation (staging, a break, anything that cuts a tree) the piece that holds the craft's root part keeps the craft; every other piece that takes parts of it away is a NEW craft with the id <parent craft id>.<instance id of its root part> and CraftRuntime.parent = the craft it left. The lineage is the parent craft id and nothing else: no separation tick is kept beyond the piece's joinedTick. The VESSEL id of one piece craft keeps its derived form <launched craft>~<instance id of its root part>; it is not its craft id. Re-docking former pieces of one craft is ORDINARY DOCKING: two craft and a link through your capture and hard-dock path; never merge them back into one tree and never special-case a pair because of its lineage. An issued craft id, a vehicle id and an instance id contain none of '/', '~' and '.'; outside its craft a part is named by the part key craftId/instanceId, and your events (dockCapture, docked, captureLost, undocked, collision) carry part keys always (the v1 events follow at the tighten step after sub-wave 3.2). No code takes an id apart: the lineage is a field (CraftRuntime.parent, CraftSnapshot.parent). CREW FLAG: the vessel's crewAlive is DERIVED from its command parts at every merge and every split (crewAliveOf), never copied from one of the vessels involved, and the g dose lives on the command part, so it stays with its crew through docking and undocking: a merge does not hand one craft's dose or loss to another craft's crew, and after a split each piece has the flag of the command parts it holds. LAUNCH SEQUENCE (ARCHITECTURE 7.2, 7.5; lead decision): a vehicle whose file mates several craft trees by docking ports (a stack that launches pre-docked) is several craft from its first tick; it has ONE stage list in its file while each craft fires only the actions on its own parts, and today a pilot's stage() reaches the helm craft only, so such a vehicle cannot be flown through the session yet (no existing vehicle is affected: meridian-lunar is one tree). The rule: the vehicle file's stage list is a launch sequence, one ordered sequence across the vehicle's own craft, compiled at assembly into entries that name their craft; the stage command of the pilot at the helm walks that sequence for as long as every craft it names is still in the pilot's assembly and owned by that pilot; an entry whose craft has left the assembly (undocked, separated, or handed to another owner) is skipped, and from then on each craft's own stack applies, as ARCHITECTURE 7.5 already says for docked craft of different owners. YOU implement the walk in the helm rules, with a test on a pre-mated two-craft vehicle (test-tandem of tests/unit/sim-vessel/dockingFixtures.ts): one pilot flies it through every entry of the sequence with the stage command alone; after an undock of the second craft, and after its hand-over to another owner, its entries are skipped by the helm pilot's stage command and fire from that craft's own stack. fleet-data writes vehicles to this rule and its validateVehicle checks it.

workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: ARCHITECTURE sections 6.1, 6.2, 6.5, 7.2, 10.5, 13, 15 (all of it: it is your specification), 16 (all four parts: the stage ladder, which roles share a process at which stage, stage 0 in detail, the local stack), 25, 26, 27, 28.2 (lane equivalence), 28.4, 28.6, 29.2, 30, docs/research/v2/hosting-small.md sections 3, 4, 5 and 8 (what must still happen when nobody plays, the measured memory floor, stage 0, the local stack), docs/research/v2/hosting.md sections 3.1, 6, 8, docs/research/v2/proposal-server-simulates.md sections 6, 7, docs/research/v2/proposal-adaptive-balance.md sections 7, 8, docs/handoff/universe-directory.md, docs/handoff/island-core.md (island codec), docs/handoff/wire-protocol.md (the session layer and its transcripts), docs/handoff/platform-delivery.md (the image and its buildId, the local stack launcher and its role manifest, the compose form, and the stage-0 measurements: billed memory, the deploy overlap and drain, a Postgres restart, the derating), docs/handoff/solar-system-sim.md (the shared tile store interface).

PROVIDED BY THE LEAD: pg and its types and embedded-postgres (installed since wave 3); the sizing settings from the wave-3 measurements (replica limits, the stage-0 admission cap, the tile-store cap). One Node program, roles by configuration, thin around src/universe: sockets, threads, Postgres, buckets. No game rule lives in server/. THE SAME ROLES RUN IN TWO SHAPES, and both are deployment stages (ARCHITECTURE 16.2): COMBINED, one game process holding gateway, directory, API and publisher on its main thread with the shard's worker isolates as its threads (this is what production runs first, on the Hobby plan, adding about $10-25 a month at 5 players), and SPLIT, gate, dir (carrying api and pub) and sim-k as separate processes over TCP (stage 2; the local stack's --shape=split is gate, dir+api+pub, sim-1 and sim-2). A third wiring, LAUNCH (api and pub as their own processes, two gateways; --shape=launch), is smoke-tested so that stage 3 is not first wired in production. There is one execution path: a role never asks which shape it is in, only the role wiring does. Every suite below runs in both shapes unless it says otherwise. You own src/net this sub-wave and answer wire-layer requests from netcode-client; THE SESSION PROTOCOL EXISTS ONCE: your gateway runs the server half of the session layer of src/net and your tests replay its transcripts; you do not write a second handshake. Everything is built and verified on the local stack (ARCHITECTURE 16.4), with no cloud resource: by default npm run stack, HOST Node processes and the embedded Postgres 18 (you add the game roles to platform-delivery's role manifest; you own deploy/local this sub-wave; the program entry hands your HTTP roles the egress meter, and server/ never imports deploy/); THE RESTART, RECOVERY, KILL, DUMP AND BILLED-MEMORY ROWS RUN INSIDE THE PINNED LINUX IMAGE through docker compose (a Node process on Windows cannot receive SIGTERM from another process, host Node is not the build journal replay is defined on, the embedded Windows bundle has no pg_dump, and container memory is what Railway bills); drain is also reachable by a control message, which is what the host stack uses. The stack never runs in the background: every suite runs as npm run stack -- [options] -- <suite>, which holds the one stack slot for that suite (rule 5). YOU ARE THE ONLY IMPLEMENTER OF THE PUBLISHER (ARCHITECTURE 13.1, 16.1): platform-delivery did not write one; the module that runs inside game and inside dir is the one that ROLES=pub starts as its own service later. Deployment is wave 6.

SCOPE:
- Role wiring: one message schema between roles over MessagePort in one process and a length-prefixed TCP stream between services, BATCHED: one frame per gateway process per shard per control tick in each direction, one batch (or a SharedArrayBuffer ring) per worker per tick between a shard's main thread and its workers. Which roles a process runs is configuration (ROLES=game, or gate, dir+api+pub, sim, or api and pub each alone); the combined process and the split are both production shapes. A role in standby refuses a connection at once with the reason standby, so that a client moves to the next candidate of the endpoint document (ARCHITECTURE 13.1). Main-thread utilisation of game, and of every shard and of the directory in the split, is a metric: it is the trigger for moving to stage 2.
- THE IDLE STATE (ARCHITECTURE 6.2): when the last island is gone and the last grace, hold and pad slot has ended, the tick loop stops; what remains on a timer is the lease renewal (one UPDATE every 5 s over one connection), a metrics sample every 30 s and ONE timer for the earliest horizon_tick on the live or a cohort clock (a fate: a worker and the terrain it needs are ready 60 s before it, the run is flown, the process goes idle again); HOW MUCH STAYS RESIDENT IS THE SETTING idleLevel: WARM (the default; stages 0 to 2) keeps one worker isolate and the resident pyramids of the bodies that have launch sites, and releases every other residency and every tile-store entry beyond those pyramids ten minutes after the last island left; LIGHT (the extra shards of stage 3) also terminates the worker isolates and releases every residency; the expiry sweep is due every 60 s but is skipped while no session is open and no document is requested and runs first, before the answer, when the next request arrives; public documents are built on request and cached for a second; partitions are created with the first island. Nothing is suspended and nothing needs waking: at the warm level the first Deploy after a quiet spell finds its worker and its terrain already there; at the light level it starts a worker isolate and loads the body's resident pyramid, within 3 s.
- Gateway: WebSocket accept (on the main thread of game in the combined shape; cluster processes in the split), the session layer (Hello/Challenge/Auth/Welcome, session tokens, resume before new sessions, takenOver), subscriptions, fan-out of island frames encoded once by the shard and of the relevant set, per-client budget and drop-superseded, input routing, the 5 s input buffer per island WITH THE ACKNOWLEDGED TICKS and the last frame tick forwarded to each client, declared socket loss (1 s ping, 3 s), rate limits (60 inputs/s, 20 commands/s, the stamp bound, the Time-request limits of ARCHITECTURE 26).
- Directory host: runs the universe's directory with real wall time and up-time; THE LEASE (a Postgres advisory lock plus a row whose fencing token is checked in every write transaction; a second instance passes its health check in standby, loads nothing and writes nothing until it holds the lease; the old one's writes fail once the token moves); island placement and epochs; heartbeats and fencing; reservations in memory, re-asserted by holders on re-registration; screening and forecast chains on helper threads; admission from measured p99 step time and never beyond the configured admission cap (20 at stage 0); the expiry sweep (on demand while idle, as above); the public documents (live.json, status.json, per-SOI census snapshot and deltas) built at most once a second and only while somebody asks, handed to pub, each carrying pollAfterS; A POSTGRES RESTART UNDER A LIVE DIRECTORY (the lease session is gone: freeze every clock at the next tick boundary, Notice recovering, keep the unwritten batch, reconnect with backoff, take the lease again after checking that no other holder wrote, write the kept batch once, resume at the frozen tick).
- Shard host: worker threads, one isolate each with its own DefLibrary, STARTED ON DEMAND (one is kept while idle at the warm level, more are started as the step-time budget requires up to the configured count, 2 at stage 0; the extra ones are terminated when the last island is gone, and all of them at the light level); tick scheduling by SLEEPING to the next boundary, never spinning; the real-time lane and THE TRAILING-LANE EXECUTOR against universe-directory's scheduler interface (lagCap stays 0 by default); islands migrate by value (island codec) between workers and shards of one build; timers (latch, dead-man, helm, grace) turned into tick-stamped inputs; frame encoding; the height authority with LAZY PER-BODY RESIDENCY and ONE SHARD-WIDE DECODED-TILE STORE in SharedArrayBuffers read by every isolate (cap configurable: 256 MB at stage 0, 512 MB at stage 1 once the limits are raised, 1 GB on the stage-2 shard, 2.5 GB at launch; entries outside the resident pyramids that no island has touched for ten minutes are released; 32 MB collision memo per worker), over the pack source reading ranges straight into the store, with NO on-disk cache by default (Railway bills page cache as memory; the disk LRU is a setting, off unless measured bucket latency asks for it); checkpoints (island codec) and journal chunks sent to the directory; flush-now for destructive outcomes between two owners.
- Persistence: the schema of ARCHITECTURE 15.2 with migrations (reserved state, tombstones and lineage, codec_version and defs_hash, slot_account, lease, usage_hour, meta.change_seq); A START CHECK that refuses a database whose server_encoding is not UTF8 or whose datlocprovider is not the built-in one (ARCHITECTURE 15.2: the local cluster and Railway's are created alike); THE CONNECTION POOLS of 15.3 (at most 4 per directory process: the lease session, the batch writer, a reader, a spare; max_connections is 40); the single writer (a database worker thread; 250 ms batches; commit-before-release for two-owner transitions with the island checkpoint AND the journal chunk up to the transition tick in one transaction); island_jrnl and island_ckpt INSERT-ONLY and partitioned (hour; five minutes), partitions dropped by the retention rule, nothing rewritten in place; event_log partitioned by day and kept 30 days (a setting); everything sized for the 5 GB volume of stage 0 (WAL capped at 256 MB; report table and WAL size); THE DUMP (ARCHITECTURE 15.3): the hourly job of platform-delivery gets its real content from you: everything except island_jrnl, island_ckpt and usage_hour, skipped when meta.change_seq has not moved since the last dump (you increment it in every batch that writes anything but the lease row and usage_hour: the lease is rewritten every 5 s, so a test on the WAL position or the transaction counter would never skip and an empty universe would upload 24 dumps a day), triggered once more at the end of a rollout's flush, with the retention of 24 hourly, 14 daily and 8 weekly copies and the upload budget that lengthens the interval; on Hobby this dump is the only copy outside the volume, so its restore is tested; restore tool; the journal-off switch; THE DECODE SWEEP at start (every stored dyn and checkpoint decodes under the current library through the migration registry, or the lobby stays closed and the rows are named).
- Recovery (ARCHITECTURE 15.4), which holds in both shapes; the shape only decides which roles can fail separately: graceful drain for the rollout sequence (freeze at a tick, final checkpoints, flush, lease release), which for the combined game is a DEPLOY OVERLAP (the new process healthy in standby, the old one draining on SIGTERM inside 45 s, the new one taking the lease) and for the split the ordered sequence; THE STAGE MOVE from combined to split on a live database (game drains and releases the lease, dir takes it and runs the decode sweep, sim-1 restores the islands from the checkpoints of the same build); in the combined shape a WORKER ISOLATE dying is the single-shard case (the directory and the input buffer survive in the main thread) and the GAME PROCESS dying is the whole-universe crash; whole-universe crash: EACH ISLAND RESTORED AT ITS OWN DURABLE TICK, never earlier; a clock resumes at the minimum and an island ahead of it is held; an island more than 1 s behind goes behind; the resume window (30 s, 90 s on a build change) holding the live and cohort clocks; NON-QUIESCENT ISLANDS HELD until their pilots have resumed or the grace has ended, U16 timers starting then; single-shard loss: restore, replay the gateway-buffered inputs with their acknowledged ticks only up to the last frame tick a client was sent, then hold for the pilots; DIRECTORY RESTART WITH LIVE SHARDS: shards freeze at the next tick boundary, keep unacknowledged chunks, transitions and reservations, re-register by (island id, epoch, durable tick) and re-send idempotently; only an unknown epoch restores from checkpoint; build-id check (no journal replay and no island migration across builds; checkpoints and dyn are migrated).
- API: account create/recover/rename/delete with per-IP limits and slow-hashed recovery codes, bulk account provisioning with an operator token and THE OPERATOR FAULT COMMANDS (exit the process without draining; terminate worker isolate k), both behind ONE operator switch that is on for rehearsal environments and the local stack only and never on production (a service restart on Railway is a SIGTERM with the drain, so the load test can produce a crash no other way); the admission cap is a setting that the same switch allows to be lifted; lobby list, token-protected metrics (Prometheus text) and an /ops page (record ids and island hashes for the production acceptance; the game's own cost lines and egress budgets and the stage triggers the game can measure, each with its current value and threshold; the workspace reading that deploy/stage.mjs status --push posts, shown with its date; and a plain statement of the lines /ops cannot see: Postgres, shell, the dump job, the volume, the buckets, the workspace's other project), the pack list presigned on the packs bucket with the date quantised to the UTC day and a 7-day lifetime, carrying the mirror's mode and slice size, the planning endpoint (the same pure functions as the client's providers, cached per vessel and target revision). pub, THE ONE PUBLISHER: serves the documents the directory hands it with explicit Cache-Control, pollAfterS (4 s, stretched to 30 s above the request budget) and 429 with Retry-After beyond four times the budget; and THE BYTE BUDGETS of ARCHITECTURE 13.1 and 16.2, counted per route with the egress meter and reset at 00:00 UTC, each a setting: anonymous public documents 2 GB a day (pollAfterS at its maximum from half of it, 429 once it is spent), anonymous API routes 1 GB a day, a per-address limit on both; a request that carries a live session token is served outside the anonymous budget, so a player in flight keeps the census.
- Observability per ARCHITECTURE 27: structured logs under 500 lines per second per process, per-second metrics from every role including resident memory and tile-store size per shard; THE COST NUMBERS: memory as billed (the container's cgroup memory.current, page cache included, where a cgroup exists), vCPU-seconds, egress bytes per route (sockets, documents, the API), and from them the game's own month-to-date usage at list prices and its projection, accumulated in usage_hour in the normal batch and read back at start, so that a rollout or a crash does not reset the month; the lines the roles cannot see are labelled as such on /ops and come from deploy/stage.mjs status. NO ALERT ROUTING: nothing posts anywhere; thresholds are shown beside their metrics on /ops.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/net/server; transcripts and a wire-level client built on the session layer's client half; the rollout, overlap, kill, restart, dump and memory rows in the pinned Linux image through compose, the rest on the host stack; BOTH SHAPES unless a row names one):
- IDLE, measured in the pinned image (cgroup memory.current, the number Railway bills), at BOTH levels. Fifteen minutes after the last client left, at the WARM level game has no tick timer, one worker isolate and only the launch bodies' resident pyramids (asserted from its metrics), at most 0.7 GB and 0.02 vCPU averaged over 10 minutes, and the first Deploy after the spell has control-enabled no later than on a busy server; at the LIGHT level it has no worker isolate and no resident terrain, at most 0.45 GB, and the first Deploy has control-enabled within 3 s of what a busy server takes. Postgres stays inside a 0.5 GB container limit through an hour of lease writes and three dump runs. A fate whose horizon falls inside the idle spell is still flown on time; an expiry that fell due during the spell is applied before the first document is answered.
- COST PROJECTION, measured in the pinned image at list prices by the one formula of ARCHITECTURE 29.2 (U is the game's own usage projected to 730 hours; the ceilings are judged on U + $5): idle, U + $5 at most $30; and 5 wire-level clients flying the normal mix for 30 minutes at most 0.75 GB and 0.15 vCPU for game and 0.5 GB for Postgres, which with their measured socket bytes gives U + $5 of at most $50; the hand-off prints both projections line by line against the estimates of U ($5-15 idle, $10-25 at 5 players). A miss is the first line of the hand-off.
- Rollout sequence during an ascent, a coast and with a parked three-craft assembly (fixtures, marked seeded): every vessel identical by island hash afterwards; clocks resume at their stored ticks after the resume window; the live clock did not advance while down; the ascending island is held until its client resumes and its throttle is where the client left it; freeze duration reported; peak Postgres connections during the overlap at most 12.
- TWO DIRECTORY PROCESSES overlapping for 20 s (two game processes in the combined shape, exactly as a Railway deploy overlaps them; two dir processes in the split): the standby writes nothing; the old one's writes fail once the lease moves; no row written twice (200 seeded hand-over points).
- THE STAGE MOVE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, combined to split and split back to combined, on a live database with an ascent in progress and a three-craft assembly parked: every vessel identical by island hash, the ascending island held for its client, the freeze under 40 s plus the resume window, reported. THE CLIENT IS GIVEN NO ADDRESS: it holds the stack's endpoint document, which the harness changes before the freeze (the new service first, the old one second), it is refused with standby until the new gateway accepts, and it resumes there inside the 30 s resume window without a reload. The two-client docking line also passes once in --shape=launch.
- COMBINED SHAPE: a worker isolate killed during an ascent: its islands restored by another isolate within 10 s for 100 islands and replayed only to the last sent frame from the surviving input buffer; SIGKILL of the game process during an ascent, a reservation, a claim commit and a dock, in 200 seeded kill points: each island back at its own durable tick with at most 250 ms re-run, every two-owner transition fully applied or absent and never rolled back once its event was released, flights held for their clients.
- POSTGRES RESTARTED under a live directory during an ascent and during a dock commit (both shapes): clocks freeze, the lease is taken again with a higher token, the kept batch is written exactly once, nothing is rolled back; the freeze equals the database's restart time plus at most 2 s.
- SPLIT SHAPE: SIGKILL of a shard during an ascent: islands recovered on another shard within 10 s for 100 islands, at most 250 ms lost, replayed only to the last sent frame, held for their clients, then behind and rejoined by jump; SIGKILL of the directory during a reservation, a claim commit and a dock, and with a staging split inside the lost batch: shards freeze and re-register, the split's records exist with the same ids, the transition is fully applied or absent and never rolled back once its event was released (record counts and craft ids checked) in 200 seeded kill points; a shard frozen for 5 s after its islands were recovered has every write, frame and event rejected.
- LANE EQUIVALENCE AND MIGRATION: one recorded input log through the real-time lane, the trailing lane in batches of 30 and 240 ticks, and a mid-flight migration between workers gives identical island hashes; an input late by less than L costs no correction (acknowledged at its stamped tick).
- Decode sweep: a database written by the previous codec version and under a changed part definition opens after migration; a planted undecodable row keeps the lobby closed and is named. Restore from the bucket dump into an empty database reproduces every passive record.
- Expiry with an injected wall clock on the staging rules: every row of ARCHITECTURE 15.5 fires with the right reason, including unowned-attached craft, the anchor passing, whole-assembly removal and the pressure rule; attended and reserved vessels never expire; up-time timers (pad reservation, helm request, grace) do not run across a 40 s outage.
- Memory (cgroup memory.current in the pinned image, inside the 6 GB Docker VM): the combined game process at most 0.75 GB with 5 clients and a 256 MB tile store, and 1.6 GB with 50 and a 512 MB store, inside its 2 GB limit (the store cap honoured, idle entries released); A SHARD OF 2 AND OF 4 WORKERS with islands on four bodies: memory per worker isolate (budget 200 MB), of the shard's main thread and of the shared store, reported separately, from which the stage-2 shard (about 2 GB) and the 22-worker shard (budget 7.4 GB) are DERIVED and marked derived (a 22-worker shard fits neither the VM nor this machine's bounds, and is measured whole only in the launch rehearsal); a body's pyramid is released when its last island leaves.
- COMBINED SHAPE under load on one machine (the host stack's LOAD PROFILE, --profile=load: servers at most 4 GB, clients at most 2 GB, started only with 16 GB of physical memory free and nothing else heavy beside it; ARCHITECTURE 16.4; the 1.5 and 2.5 GB bounds are those of the acceptance profile), 5, 50 and 200 wire-level clients: main-thread utilisation of game per connected client (the number that sets the stage-2 trigger and the admission caps), step time, bytes per client per tier, batch commit latency p99; the publisher under 500 polling menu clients: pollAfterS stretches, 429 beyond the request budget and once the daily byte budget is spent, requests with a live session still served, socket traffic unaffected.
- 500 wire-level clients on one machine, split shape, in the load profile (the same bound): gateway CPU per connection, bytes per client per tier, shard and directory main-thread utilisation, batch commit latency p99, table and WAL size after 30 minutes with partitions dropping, directory transitions per second reported; no reliable frame dropped; idle shard CPU near zero (sleep scheduling).
- THE OPERATOR SWITCH: with it off (as on production) bulk provisioning, the fault commands and a lifted admission cap are refused; with it on, exit-without-drain and terminate-worker produce the crash rows above. The start check refuses a WIN1252 cluster; a ship name with characters outside Windows-1252 round-trips; callsign uniqueness is case-insensitive.
- No secret in the repository; the client bundle contains no server code (boundary test); server/ imports nothing from deploy/.

Never run npm install: the dependencies and configuration entries you need are listed under PROVIDED BY THE LEAD in your brief, or are a request. (6) Git: only git add <your paths>, then commit; never add -A, stash, reset, rebase, amend or push (releases are tags the lead moves); commit working states often. (7) Write files with the Write tool, absolute paths. (8) Secrets (.env, provider tokens) are read only at run time by tools under tools/, server/, bots/ or deploy/; never printed, committed, logged in a URL or shipped to the client; run node tools/dev/check-secrets.mjs before every commit if you touch them. (9) Cloud: never touch existing Modal apps or volumes or the existing Railway project; create cloud resources only when your brief names them, only in the Railway project fable-space-program and the Modal environment fsp (both approved by the user: docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS_V2.md, Answered), on the Railway HOBBY plan and inside the stage-0 limits of ARCHITECTURE 16.2; anything that needs the Pro plan, raises the standing spend or is a rehearsal beyond what the Hobby plan allows is the lead's to announce to the user first: stop and ask the lead. Everything else is built and verified on the local stack, which needs no cloud resource; never report a local-stack result as a deployed or measured-capacity result. workPackages.title: NetSession: the predicting replica, reconciliation, client stores, the planning providers and their chooser, identity key and reconnect
workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: ARCHITECTURE sections 5.2, 5.4, 6.2-6.4, 13, 14, 15.4 (what a client sees after a recovery), 17, 25, docs/research/v2/proposal-server-simulates.md section 4.6-4.8, docs/research/v2/proposal-adaptive-balance.md section 5.5-5.7, docs/research/v2/frontend-ux.md sections 5.17, 6, docs/handoff/universe-directory.md, docs/handoff/island-core.md, docs/handoff/wire-protocol.md (the session layer: use its client half), docs/handoff/solar-system-sim.md (the planning functions).

You make a remote universe feel local. The server process is being built beside you this sub-wave, so you test against an in-process UniverseHost wrapped in the SERVER HALF of the session layer of src/net (wire-protocol built both halves and their transcripts): the handshake, resume, subscriptions, budget and input buffer you talk to are the real ones, not a fake gateway of your own. The first run against the real server is the net-joint-gate package after you. Requests against src/sim, src/universe and src/session go to contact-docking (the owner this sub-wave); against server/ and src/net to server-persistence. Anything that needs vessel contact (collisions, capture) is out of your acceptance and is proven in net-joint-gate.

SCOPE:
- NetSession implements FlightSession (src/client/net): session handshake, time sync, the client's copy of its clock schedule, the replica (the island code in predict mode) running ahead by half the round trip plus the jitter buffer (adapted from input margin, capped at 250 ms, never predicting beyond 500 ms), input sampling on control ticks with stamped ticks, a one-second ring of inputs and codec copies of island state, comparison with tolerance (0.2 mm, 0.2 mm/s, 2e-5 rad), restore-and-replay with other pilots' reported controls, visual error offsets in the island frame decaying over 150 ms, RESYNCED above 5 m. InputAck: replay with the tick each input was applied at; a late command is re-timed (a correction), never a reversal. IslandOp handling: roll back to the op's tick, apply with the server's ids, replay; replace on checksum mismatch. IslandEnter is the island codec (tiers, nascent and U5 pairs, constraints). The presentation rule of ARCHITECTURE 6.4 exactly: own command-triggered structure in a single-owner island at once ONLY while the measured input margin is positive for the stamped tick, otherwise on the server's operation; events newer than the Durable tick carry provisional; threshold outcomes and anything touching another owner's craft only on the server's event; CommandResult pending states.
- Rails: evaluate the clock schedule and conics locally; never draw past untilTick; the stop window of U7 (stamp rate changes with the displayed tick).
- Near tier (integrated islands, Reduced-tier debris, unattended runs) drawn by blending between osculating conics with a 150 ms delay, so a spent stage stays visible and continuous after it leaves the island; the relevant-set store from the socket and the census store from the public documents (HTTP snapshot plus sequence-numbered deltas, polled at 1 Hz only while the map is open), both with solid/echo classification from the entry (head, horizon, forecast chain validity, reservation, clock id) and the own clock; a solid vessel is never chained on the client: its patches come from the server; worldline fetch for the relevant set; TimeView, presence and timeOffset in snapshots; the SimSnapshot built by src/sim/view from replica state plus local planning state (nodes saved to the server as an opaque Plan).
- ClientStores filled from messages and from live.json polling (pads, ships, assembly, roster, rules, presence, feed, prompts, link state); the poller obeys the pollAfterS field of each public document and Retry-After on 429 (ARCHITECTURE 13.1), keeping the last document meanwhile; weak-client mode from cpuScore.
- PlanningService (session.ts) providers and their chooser (src/client/planning): in-process for Node and bots, a planning worker in the browser, and the API's endpoint; the chooser is the table of UniverseRules (worker under the estimate threshold or with the link down; cache when the key exists; endpoint for a client under weakClientCpuScore or above the threshold); results keyed by vessel and target revision, never blocking a frame. The map and the HUD consume only the interface.
- Clock states for the player: held, behind (with the one-key rejoin jump), resume window, guest or bound, the offers by relation after a lost claim, RANGE: CLEARING.
- Identity (src/client/identity): non-extractable ECDSA P-256 key in IndexedDB, challenge signing, recovery-code entry, storage persistence request, duplicate-tab detection.
- THE ENDPOINT DOCUMENT (ARCHITECTURE 13.1; src/client/endpoints): the client has no server address compiled in. It is given the URL of /endpoints.json and nothing else; it reads { v, build, gate[], api[], pub[], bootPack }, each list ordered candidates, tries the candidates of a list in order, treats a refusal with the reason standby as next candidate, now, and READS THE DOCUMENT AGAIN BEFORE EVERY RECONNECT ATTEMPT and on 429, 5xx or a network failure from the publisher or the API, so that a stage move or a new pub service needs no reload. Bots and tests use the same reader.
- Reconnect: backoff with jitter, the endpoint document re-read first, resume, rebuild from IslandEnter, hidden-tab keep-alive from a worker, takenOver, version mismatch.
- window.__test.net(): round trip, input margin, corrections (count, size), bytes per tier, durable tick.

ACCEPTANCE (headless NetSession bots with the scripted pilots, injector profiles 0, 50, 150, 300 ms and 5 % stalls of 200 ms):
- Solo ascent to orbit, entry and a lunar touchdown at 150 ms: no correction above tolerance outside the first second after a stall; correction count and size per latency reported; at 300 ms with stalls the flight still completes.
- ZERO REVERSALS in 1,000 seeded runs of staging, overheating at the limit and a hard landing at crash tolerance, at every latency profile including 200 ms stalls (assert on the event stream the view emits); a stalled stage command is re-timed and counted as a correction, and the pieces never rejoin on screen.
- Observed flight (no contact needed): client B watching client A's ascent with staging from a neighbouring pad and a burn at 500 m and 5 km draws A within the bounds of ARCHITECTURE 13.5 per tier against the server's state at the same tick; throttle and ignition within the stated delay; each staging event once; each spent stage visible and continuous in chase view to impact or expiry.
- Planning: a client under the weak-client threshold shows the same closest approaches as local computation (1 m, 0.1 s); the endpoint's p95 latency and cache hit rate reported (against the in-process API handler); no main-thread task above 1 ms from planning.
- Recovery code and identity (unit, fake IndexedDB): a new device key bound by the code sees the same account; the old code is refused; the ephemeral-profile warning fires before the first ship.
- Two NetSessions in one island: both draw both vessels at the same predicted tick; a 0.04 m/s^2 RCS input by one is mispredicted by the other by less than 1 mm at 150 ms.
- Warp at 10,000,000x: a stop lands within one presentation frame of the tick displayed when the key was pressed.
- Disconnect for 5 s mid-burn: resume without RESYNCED; for 150 s: the vessel is where the unattended run left it (throttle closed after the latch). A socket lost at 10,000,000x: the clock holds at the last stamped tick. A 200 ms stall changes nothing. A hidden tab for 60 s keeps the burn. After a simulated shard recovery the island is held until the client resumes and the burn continues under the pilot's hands.
- Session cost on the main thread: p99 at most 1.5 ms per frame with two vessels; a 150 ms replay of ten vessels at most 2 ms (measured through the gate).
- Endpoint document: with the gateway list changed from [A] to [B, A] while a session is up, a socket cut makes the client read the document again, get standby from B and fall back to A; once B accepts and A has stopped, it resumes on B inside 30 s without a reload (in-process hosts behind the session layer); a 429 from the first pub candidate moves the poller to the second.
- The same client bundle runs in Node (bots) and in Chrome.

workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Until now the client was tested against an in-process host and the server against a wire-level client. They share one session layer, so they should meet without surprises; you prove it, and you fix what the meeting finds in src/client, server/ and src/net (you own them this sub-wave; a defect in src/sim or src/universe is a request the lead routes). This is a short package with a hard gate: the UI and app packages after you build on a client and a server that have flown together.

SCOPE:
- tools/net: the multi-process harness that acceptance-multiclient extends in wave 6: the roles started through the local stack (npm run stack with your own STACK_NAME: host Node processes and the embedded Postgres, no Docker and no cloud resource) in the COMBINED shape that production runs first (one game process) and, by --shape, in the SPLIT shape (gate, dir carrying api and pub, sim-1, sim-2) and once in the LAUNCH shape (api and pub as their own processes, two gateways), and through the compose form in the pinned Linux image for the rows that kill a process or roll a deploy; EVERY CLIENT FINDS ITS GATEWAY THROUGH THE STACK'S ENDPOINT DOCUMENT (ARCHITECTURE 13.1), never by a configured address; the harness runs inside npm run stack -- [options] -- <suite>, which holds the one stack slot (rule 5); YOU OWN deploy/local THIS SUB-WAVE: you are the first package to run real clients through the launcher and the compose form with kills, a supervisor restart and a build-changing rollout, so defects of the launcher, the role manifest and compose.yml are yours to fix, not requests; a fresh database, the injector proxy per client, N headless NetSession clients with scripted pilots; collection of each client's event stream, snapshots at named ticks and net panel numbers; a mark on every run that loads vessels into the database (seeded).
- tests/net/joint, at 0 and 150 ms and with 5 % stalls of 200 ms.

ACCEPTANCE (every line from pad spawns on a fresh database unless marked):
- One client: handshake, account creation, spawn on a pad, a full ascent to orbit with staging, a 10 s disconnect mid-burn and resume, a 150 s disconnect and the unattended outcome, logout, attach to the parked ship on return (U8b).
- Two clients on neighbouring pads: both reach orbit; each sees the other's ascent within the observed-flight bounds; a collision at 20 m/s between them (ZERO reversals: neither shows damage before the server's event, both receive the same numbers; this is the collision case netcode-client could not test); a rendezvous and a hard dock by the docking pilots, undock from each side.
- The one-client and two-client lines above pass in the combined shape at both latencies, the two-client line once more in the split shape at 150 ms, and its docking part once in the launch shape.
- THE STAGE MOVE with both clients in flight, combined to split and back, in the pinned image: the endpoint document is changed before the freeze, both clients are refused with standby, resume on the new gateway inside the 30 s resume window without a reload, and their vessels are identical by island hash.
- In the pinned image, combined shape: a worker isolate killed during client A's ascent: A's island is restored, held until A resumes, and A finishes the ascent; the game process killed and restarted by its supervisor: both clients resume, at most 250 ms re-run, nothing else rolled back. Split shape: a shard killed during client A's ascent (restored, held, finished) and the directory killed and restarted: both clients continue with nothing rolled back.
- In the pinned image: the rollout with both clients in flight and a build-id change, as a deploy overlap of game and as the ordered sequence of the split: both are told to reload, resume inside the build-change grace, and their vessels are identical by island hash.
- After both clients have left and the graces have ended the server is idle (no tick timer; at the default warm level one worker isolate and the launch bodies' terrain kept): a client that then connects and deploys has control no later than on a busy server; with idleLevel light the server has no worker isolate and the client has control within 3 s more.
- The session layer has exactly one implementation: a grep proves neither src/client nor server/ parses a handshake message outside src/net.
- Measured and handed to the wave-6 packages: corrections per client-minute per latency, bytes per client per tier, the freeze durations.

(5) Shared tree: verify with scoped commands only (npm run typecheck:paths -- <paths>; npx vitest run <paths>; npx playwright test <dir>); never npm run build or npm run check; every heavy command through node tools/dev/heavy.mjs --class=<cpu|gpu|bake|stack> -- <command>, one at a time; the only client build you may run is npm run stack:client (the lead's; it writes under data/stack, never to dist/); THE LOCAL STACK (host Node processes and an embedded Postgres 18, no Docker; ARCHITECTURE 16.4) NEVER RUNS IN THE BACKGROUND: start it only as npm run stack -- [options] -- <your suite command> with STACK_NAME=fsp-<package id> (the script takes the ONE stack slot of heavy.mjs, brings the stack up, runs your command with STACK_URL and STACK_ENDPOINTS set, and stops the stack when the command exits; a command inside it that needs the GPU is itself wrapped in heavy.mjs --class=gpu); hold the slot for one suite at a time and release it between suites, because other packages wait for it; the docker compose form (the pinned Linux image) is the same command with --compose, in the same slot, only for the suites your brief names, and it stops what it started, a Docker daemon included; never leave a server, database, browser or container running. (6) Git: only git add <your paths>, then commit; never add -A, stash, reset, rebase, amend or push (releases are tags the lead moves); commit working states often. (7) Write files with the Write tool, absolute paths. (8) Secrets (.env, provider tokens) are read only at run time by tools under tools/, server/, bots/ or deploy/; never printed, committed, logged in a URL or shipped to the client; run node tools/dev/check-secrets.mjs before every commit if you touch them. (9) Cloud: never touch existing Modal apps or volumes or the existing Railway project; create cloud resources only when your brief names them, only in the Railway project fable-space-program and the Modal environment fsp (both approved by the user: docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS_V2.md, Answered), on the Railway HOBBY plan and inside the stage-0 limits of ARCHITECTURE 16.2; anything that needs the Pro plan, raises the standing spend or is a rehearsal beyond what the Hobby plan allows is the lead's to announce to the user first: stop and ask the lead. Never build alert routing and never ask for a webhook. Everything else is built and verified on the local stack, which needs no cloud resource; never report a local-stack result as a deployed or measured-capacity result. (10) Browser work: real Chrome, real GPU, assert the adapter, close loops on state, LOOK at every screenshot you save; perf only under the GPU lock; where your brief names reference images, compare with the helper in tests/browser/harness.ts and never re-record one yourself. (11) Disk: data/ stays under 22 GB, data/packs under 20 GB, at least 25 GB of the disk free; delete intermediates. (12) Finish with docs/handoff/<package id>.md: public API with exact signatures, how to run and verify, measured numbers against every acceptance criterion (say plainly which were not met and why), known limits, and every contract change you request.

workPackages.title: Deployment of stage 0 to Railway (Hobby plan) and Modal; rollout, the stage ladder scripts and the scale controller; the bot fleet; the cost readings and the load tests with simulated active players; the capacity and cost report; production acceptance
workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: ARCHITECTURE sections 5.9, 6.2 (the idle state and its levels), 9.3, 10.4, 13.1 (the endpoint document, the publisher's budgets), 15.3, 15.4, 16 (all: the stage ladder is your specification), 27, 28.6, 28.7 (the three programmes), 29.2, 30, 31.4 (Deployed), docs/research/v2/hosting-small.md (all: the Hobby plan's limits, stage 0, the scale-up steps; its cost table is superseded by the table of ARCHITECTURE 30, which is the one you replace with measurements), docs/research/v2/hosting.md sections 3, 8-12, docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS_V2.md (what is answered; Q2, Q5, Q6 and Q19 with what the lead has recorded under them), docs/handoff/server-persistence.md, docs/handoff/netcode-client.md, docs/handoff/net-joint-gate.md, docs/handoff/platform-delivery.md (the stage-0 skeleton that already runs, its measured idle usage, the overlap and drain timings, the derating), docs/capacity/*.

You put the game on the internet and measure what it holds and what it costs. "Architecture alone isn't proof of capacity": the deliverable is a deployed game and a report with measured limits. THE USER'S DECISION SHAPES THIS PACKAGE: the always-on deployment is STAGE 0 on the Railway HOBBY plan (one game process, shell, Postgres, the dump job, two buckets), it must cost about $50 a month or less at about 5 concurrent players and about $30 or less with nobody connected (judged by the one formula of ARCHITECTURE 29.2; the workspace's other project already uses the plan's included $5, so the game's usage is billed in full), and it grows by configuration and deploys only on measured need. You own server/ and src/net this wave for operational and performance fixes (behaviour changes only with a test that shows the defect). acceptance-multiclient works in parallel on the simulation and the client: you measure only TAGGED builds (the lead moves the release tag and the release branch; nobody pushes main; fixes are merged between ramps), every report row names its build, and the highest level that held is re-run on the final build. Use your own STACK_NAME; only one local stack runs at a time, so every local suite runs as npm run stack -- [options] -- <suite> and you release the slot between suites (acceptance-multiclient waits for it). Print the cumulative spend after every run.

WHAT YOU MAY SPEND. The Railway project, the Modal environment and stage 0 are approved (OPEN_QUESTIONS, Answered): programme 1 of ARCHITECTURE 28.7 is NOT optional, fits the Hobby plan and costs a few dollars. Programmes 2 and 3 (the stage-up drill, the split, the launch rehearsal) need the Pro plan and the user's yes, and the user is asked with YOUR numbers, so there is a FIXED CHECKPOINT (ARCHITECTURE 28.7): when programme 1 ends you write docs/capacity/<date>-stage0.md (the two cost readings, the measured limit of stage 0 and what broke first, the pad cycle, the price of programmes 2 and 3 from ARCHITECTURE 30) and file docs/requests/deploy-loadtest-q19.md for the lead; the lead puts OPEN_QUESTIONS Q19 to the user and records the answer and its time there. While you wait you do the rest of your scope (the stage scripts and their dry runs, the split and launch shapes on the local stack, the production acceptance). You run programmes 2 and 3 ONLY once Q19 records that the user agreed and that the workspace is on Pro; on a no, or with no answer 48 hours after your request, you finish with their scripts, dry runs and local runs, and the report says in its first lines that the larger stages are estimates. A yes that arrives after you have finished re-opens this brief for those two programmes before final-gate. If the game cannot be deployed or the bots cannot run for a reason outside your control, do everything else, then STOP AND REPORT A BLOCKER: the hand-off's first line is "NOT DEPLOYED" with the completion criteria of PROMPT.txt that are therefore unmet (the deployed multiplayer experience, measured load limits, persistence proven on the deployed game). A local-stack pass is never reported as done.

SCOPE:
- Deployment of STAGE 0 (ARCHITECTURE 16.2), filling platform-delivery's skeleton in the Railway project fable-space-program, environment production (rules/default.json): game (ROLES=game: gate, dir, api and pub in one process with up to 2 worker isolates, a 256 MB tile store and idleLevel warm; built by Railway from the release branch with the Dockerfile, or from an uploaded export of the tag while the GitHub App has no access, OPEN_QUESTIONS Q5; autodeploy OFF; standby-aware health check; RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS=45; restart policy Always; replica limit 2 vCPU / 2 GB; ADMISSION_CAP=20), shell (static and packs, CDN on, autodeploy on its watch paths with Wait for CI, limit 0.5 vCPU / 0.25 GB), postgres (18, created UTF8 with the built-in locale by platform-delivery, 5 GB volume, limit 1 vCPU / 0.5 GB, max_connections 40), the hourly dump job with its retention and its upload budget, the two buckets (packs: credential in game and shell; dumps: credential only in the dump job and the Modal secret), the endpoint document on shell listing game for gate, api and pub, the egress budgets of ARCHITECTURE 16.2 as variables, sealed variables, a rollback procedure. NO Serverless, NO hard usage limit (Railway's is per workspace), NO alert of any kind, nothing that needs Pro. The buildId of the deployed game must equal CI's for the release commit, and the boot manifest hash and the client build hash that shell reports must be the release commit's, or the rollout refuses. deploy/rollout.mjs: at stages 0 and 1 one deployment of game with the hand-over watched (healthy in standby, notice, drain inside 45 s with freeze, final checkpoints, flush and lease release, the new process takes the lease, decode sweep, restore, resume window, the dump job triggered); from stage 2 the ordered sequence for dir, sim-* and gate through the Railway API at one digest (notice, freeze, shard checkpoints, directory flush and lease release, the new directory takes the lease and runs the decode sweep, shards register, clocks resume into the resume window, gateways last, one replica at a time). THE STAGE SCRIPTS, deploy/stage.mjs, every command with a dry-run mode that prints what it would create and what it would cost per month: status (the current stage; THE WORKSPACE'S usage and estimated bill from railway usage --json and the per-project split, which is what the 0-to-1 trigger is judged on, because billing is per workspace and the roles cannot see the other project; the game's share and its projection, from Railway's figures and from the roles' own metrics; each egress budget with today's use; every trigger of the 16.2 table with its current value and threshold; the worst-case month from the replica limits, the cap and the budgets; --push posts the workspace reading to /ops through the operator API), rehearse (creates a rehearsal environment in the shape of a named stage on rules/staging.json or a load-test rule set, and deletes it at the end: nothing is left standing. Railway buckets belong to one environment, so IT GIVES THE REHEARSAL ENVIRONMENT THE PRODUCTION packs CREDENTIAL AS A SEALED VARIABLE, so that its game, shell and bots read the same immutable packs and no run uploads 14-20 GB, and NEVER the dumps credential: rehearsal dumps go to the rehearsal environment's own dumps bucket and are deleted with it. It turns on the operator switch, which enables bulk provisioning, the fault commands and a lifted admission cap, and it creates the rehearsal's operator token in Railway and in the Modal secret in the same run), up --to pro (backups and point-in-time recovery on; the source of game set to the CI image by digest, which takes effect at the next regular rollout, so the move has no rollout of its own; the volume is NOT grown: it is grown only when used space passes 4 GB, because a volume never shrinks and one above 5 GB cannot return to Hobby), up --limits (replica limits, worker count, tile-store cap, admission cap and egress budgets of game, one graceful rollout), up --pub (ROLES=pub from the same image as its own service behind the CDN, listed first in the endpoint document with game second; no freeze), up --to split (gate, dir and sim-1 created from the same digest in standby; the endpoint document changed to list gate first and game second, and the script waits until the redeployed shell serves it; the announced freeze; game drains, dir takes the lease, sim-1 restores; clients resume on gate through the document; game removed and then dropped from the document), up --to launch, and down (3 to 2: services removed after their islands have migrated; 2 to 1: the mirrored freeze; 1 to 0 only while the volume is 5 GB or smaller, otherwise it says that stage 1 is one-way). deploy/scale.mjs (adds and removes sim-k services and gateway replicas by digest; dry-run mode; prints the cost per hour) and THE SCALE CONTROLLER for stage 3 (a scheduled job reading the directory's metrics: scales out when the admission queue is above its threshold for three minutes, scales in after thirty quiet minutes, never beyond the ceiling of OPEN_QUESTIONS Q6, token as a sealed variable; it routes NO alerts: every action is logged and shown on /ops), built and tested in dry-run mode and on the launch shape of the local stack, and run live only in the launch rehearsal. The pack upload and the presigned pack list. NOTHING MOVES UP A STAGE ON PRODUCTION IN THIS PACKAGE: a move that changes the plan or raises the standing spend is announced to the user by the lead first.
- Modal (environment fsp only; nothing always on): fsp-audit (nightly replay of archived journals against committed checkpoints, on the image built from the same Dockerfile with the buildId checked first), fsp-offsite (nightly copy of the newest dump from the dumps bucket to a Modal volume: the copy off Railway; and the copy of the packs to a Modal volume through the presigned pack list, after which the lead may let data/packs be deleted), fsp-bots, fsp-probe. THE CREDENTIALS THAT LEAVE RAILWAY ARE EXACTLY THESE (ARCHITECTURE 16.2, OPEN_QUESTIONS Q5): the dumps bucket credential as a Modal secret for fsp-offsite and fsp-audit, and a rehearsal environment's operator token as a Modal secret for fsp-bots; each is written to both places by the deploy script in one run and never to a file or a log; production's operator token, the session key and the database URL never leave Railway. Releases are deployed from tags.
- Bots (bots/): headless NetSession clients driven by the generic pilots (ascent, rendezvous, docking, transfer), AT LEAST 100 per 4-core container (50 containers or fewer for 5,000; the workspace limit is shared with existing apps that must not be disturbed), EVERY bot connecting through the src/net injector with the latency mix of ARCHITECTURE 28.7 (30 % at 40 ms, 40 % at 100 ms, 20 % at 180 ms, 10 % at 280 ms; 2-5 % stalls), finding the gateway, the API and the publisher ONLY through the endpoint document (netcode-client's reader), reading height packs through the pack source as a browser does, accounts provisioned in bulk with the operator token on rehearsal environments only (the five bots of the cost reading on production create ordinary accounts and abandon their ships when the reading ends). Behaviours: launch and reach orbit, coast and WARP AS A PLAYER WOULD, rendezvous and dock with a parked station, undock, re-enter, leave mid-flight, reconnect; a share reporting a low cpuScore. Mixes: pad storm, cruise-heavy, 20 % in docking pairs, launch-day, and a VISITOR mix (menu clients polling the public documents and creating accounts). At least one bot in ten predicts fully and checks every correction; replayed input logs that end early are replaced, not counted.
- PROGRAMME 1, STAGE 0 (ARCHITECTURE 28.7; always run; Hobby). On PRODUCTION: THE IDLE FLOOR (at least 12 hours with nobody connected, TAKEN BEFORE ANY BOT HAS FLOWN ON PRODUCTION, or after the bots' ships and debris have been abandoned and removed, so that the test does not seed its own fates: usage per service and per project from Railway's usage figures for the window and from the roles' own metrics; EVERY WAKE-UP IN THE WINDOW LISTED (fates flown, document requests, sessions) and the idle state asserted between them: no tick loop, one worker isolate, only the launch bodies' resident terrain; an interval in which a stranger is connected is excluded and the window extended to keep 12 hours; projected to a month; the memory lines read AGAIN once every service has been up at least 72 hours with dump runs in the window, both readings reported, because billed memory creeps as caches fill) and THE COST AT 5 PLAYERS (5 bots in the normal mix held at least 6 hours, the same readings, projected to a month, plus the realistic pattern of four evening hours a day); the time from the first Deploy after the quiet spell to control-enabled, beside the same on a busy server; a rollout with 5 bots flying (with the peak number of Postgres connections); a Postgres restart with 5 bots flying; the cold start from a clean Chrome profile at 50 Mbit/s (bytes and seconds to the title and to the end of calibration; what the player sees meanwhile). On a REHEARSAL environment in the stage-0 shape (deploy/stage.mjs rehearse; deleted at the end): ramps of 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 bots WITH THE ADMISSION CAP LIFTED (stage 0's cap of 20 would queue every bot above 20 by configuration; admission then comes from measured step time alone, every row records the cap in force, and ONE run at the cap of 20 shows the queue and the spectating path), the levels above the 2 vCPU / 2 GB limit with the limit raised to at most 8 vCPU / 8 GB and at most 6 workers, and said so in the row: main-thread utilisation of game per connected bot, memory as billed, bytes per player as billed; STEP TIME at 1, 2, 4 and 8 synchronised workers WITH THE MAIN THREAD IDLE (eight workers under bot load beside the main thread, the database thread and the helpers on 8 vCPU would measure contention, not the workers) and at 1, 2, 4 and 6 under bot load (this replaces the derating, fixes the admission caps of stages 0 and 1 and the trigger for stage 2, and decides the shard count a launch would need; 8 and more under load belong to programmes 2 and 3); THE PAD CYCLE: the pad-storm mix on tests/load/rules/pad-scarce (the release cycle, dwell and safing values and 4 pads, which 100 to 200 bots saturate): launches per pad per hour, the distribution of the wait from Deploy to control-enabled, the bot count at which the p95 wait passes 120 s; a rollout at 20 bots and at the highest level that held; A CRASH of game and of a worker isolate at load BY THE OPERATOR FAULT COMMAND of the API (a Railway restart is a SIGTERM with the drain, which is the graceful path); THE EGRESS BUDGETS UNDER A HOSTILE CLIENT (one client looping on the mirror, on the boot pack and the hashed assets with changing query strings, and on the public documents: bytes sent per route against its budget, the answers after it, players in flight unaffected); a one-hour soak; the CHURN run; the VISITOR mix at this size (500 menu clients polling and creating accounts while 20 bots fly: the publisher's request and byte budgets, pollAfterS reached, 429s, socket traffic and requests with a live session unaffected); EXPIRY in real wall-clock time on the staging rules (a parked ship, its countdown, its removal).
- PROGRAMMES 2 AND 3 (only with the lead's record under OPEN_QUESTIONS Q19; otherwise their scripts, dry runs and local split-shape runs). Programme 2, THE STAGE-UP DRILL: a rehearsal environment walked up the ladder with 50 bots flying (0 to 1, the limits, pub behind the CDN, 1 to 2, and 2 back to 1), every step timed against the targets of ARCHITECTURE 16.2, nothing lost by island hash, THE BOTS FINDING gate AND pub ONLY THROUGH THE ENDPOINT DOCUMENT and resuming inside the resume window; then ramps of 200 and 500 on stage 2, step time at 8 synchronised workers under load, a rollout at 200, a forced shard kill and a directory kill at load. Programme 3, THE LAUNCH REHEARSAL at stage 3, Railway told before the 2,000 and 5,000 runs: ramps 1,000, 2,000, 5,000; the pad-storm and launch-day mixes on the RELEASE rule set (32 pads queueing for real); the memory of a 22-worker shard; SCALE-OUT UNDER LOAD (time from the controller's trigger to K new shards taking islands, at 500 bots; whether a project token can create services or a workspace token is needed); the visitor mix with 5,000 menu clients while 500 bots fly; the mirror's throughput as its own packs service against the numbers of ARCHITECTURE 10.4; step time at 16 and 22 synchronised workers; a rollout at 2,000; a two-hour soak.
- In every programme: each level held 15 minutes and counted only when integrated objects per connected bot meet the mix's target (0.75 normal, 1.35 launch-day); PADS AND COMPUTE SEPARATELY: the compute ramps on tests/load/rules with synthetic extra pads for the compute-limited count; the pad limit from the pad-scarce rule set in programme 1 (the measured per-pad cycle; the 32-pad figure stated as DERIVED from it, because 200 bots cannot queue 32 pads) and from pad-storm and launch-day on the release rules in programme 3 (launches per wall hour from the reservoir and sustained; median and p95 wait from Deploy to control-enabled); the soak at the highest level that held (passive count, table and WAL size over time); the CHURN run (single-launch accounts that never return, staging rules: the passive count plateaus, no spawn refused for the cap); a reconnect storm; every ROLLOUT under load with its freeze duration and nothing lost by island hash; THE BALANCE: one level repeated with lagCap = 2 s and once with 30 % low-cpuScore bots; COHERENCE in the launch-day and cruise-heavy mixes (share of attended vessels solid to another attended vessel, lead distribution, echoes against solid craft within 300 km, success rates of jump, meet and ask-to-advance; target: at least half in the launch-day mix; if missed, name the rule fields changed). Coherence needs a crowd: it is measured at the highest level each programme reaches, and the report says at which.
- The report docs/capacity/<date>-load.md. FIRST LINES: which programmes ran; the measured monthly cost of stage 0 idle and at 5 players against the two ceilings; the measured limit of stage 0 and what broke first; whether the figures for stages 2 and 3 are measured or estimates. THE COST TABLE of ARCHITECTURE 30 for stage 0 with every line measured (memory and CPU per service, socket egress, documents, boot pack, dumps, bucket, Modal), idle and at 5 players, next to the estimates, with the workspace's bill beside the game's usage, the dollars per additional concurrent player, the player count at which THE WORKSPACE'S usage reaches $20 (the Pro break-even) and at which the game alone reaches $50 a month, and the bytes each route sent against its egress budget. Then, per level and mix, with the build id: step time p50/p99/max per worker at each synchronised-worker count that ran and the knee; main-thread utilisation of game per connected bot; integrated objects per worker thread at the admission threshold and per connected bot; inputs per second per bot; billed vCPU-seconds per integrated vessel-second and idle CPU; shard and directory main-thread utilisation where they are separate; memory as billed per process; dilated and held islands; gateway CPU per connection; bytes per second per player per tier as billed; API and publisher requests per second, connections, pollAfterS reached, 429s, CDN hit rate where there is a CDN; directory transitions, screening and chain time; batch commit latency; correction rate seen by predicting bots; players when admission queues; recovery, freeze, stage-move and scale-out times; the time from idle to the first control-enabled; pad wait per level; coherence; cost of each run and cumulative. The limit per service level of 28.7, pad-limited and compute-limited stated separately; both bottleneck lists of ARCHITECTURE 29.2 (what binds on the ladder; what binds at stage 3), each line measured, or marked estimate with the programme that would measure it; the stage triggers and admission caps of ARCHITECTURE 16.2 restated from measurements; a revised cost table for the larger stages of ARCHITECTURE 30 with low and high values; the recommendation on lagCap and weakClientCpuScore with the A/B numbers behind it. The headline numbers and the wait a player can expect at the measured limit are written to the rules screen's capacity slot.

ACCEPTANCE:
- COST, FROM MEASURED USAGE ON THE DEPLOYED STAGE 0, BY THE ONE FORMULA OF ARCHITECTURE 29.2 (the user's requirement). U is the game's own usage for the window, from Railway's per-project figures cross-checked with the roles' meters, projected to 730 hours; it is what the game adds to the workspace bill and what the estimates are compared with ($5-15 idle, $10-25 at 5 players). THE CEILINGS ARE JUDGED ON U + $5, as if the game paid the whole plan fee itself: the 12-hour idle reading gives U + $5 of AT MOST ABOUT $30 A MONTH and the 6-hour reading with 5 active bots gives U + $5 of AT MOST ABOUT $50 A MONTH. The workspace's bill, max($5, U plus the other project's usage), is printed beside them. Both projections are shown line by line with the window, the raw usage figures and the arithmetic, and the idle memory lines are shown at 12 and at 72 hours of uptime. If either is missed, that is the first line of the hand-off, with the line that caused it and what would bring it under (a smaller tile store, fewer isolates, a lower send rate), and the package is not reported as complete.
- IDLE: the idle reading lists every wake-up in its window (fates, document requests, sessions); between them game ran no tick loop and held one worker isolate and only the launch bodies' resident terrain (from its metrics). A listed wake-up is not a failure; a tick loop with no cause is. Nothing was asleep: the title, live.json and status.json answered within their normal times at the end of the window, and the first Deploy had control no later than on a busy server. No service uses Serverless; no hard usage limit and no alert exists; nothing in the project needs the Pro plan. EGRESS: each budget of ARCHITECTURE 16.2 is in force on production with its documented answer once spent, and a request with a query string on a hashed route gets a 404 and no bytes.
- PRODUCTION is reachable by a stranger with the URL: the shell opens, the gate passes, a player spawns and flies; a deploy of a shell change does not touch the universe; a rollout of the simulation with 5 bots flying loses nothing (island hashes before and after), flights in progress are held for their pilots, bots resume inside the resume window, and the freeze is under 40 s plus the resume window.
- REHEARSAL (stage-0 shape): the environment read the production packs bucket and never held the dumps credential; the same rollout at 20 bots and at the highest level that held; the crash rows by the fault command; the pad cycle measured on the pad-scarce rule set; expiry demonstrated in real wall-clock time on the staging rules (a parked ship, its countdown, its removal); the environment is deleted afterwards (the project lists only production).
- PRODUCTION (rules/default.json), by a scripted two-browser run against the production URL: two vehicles spawn from pads, dock, both players log out, a simulation rollout is rolled, both resume and find the assembly intact (record ids and island hash from /ops before and after), then undock; the pack list and tiles load from a clean profile; restart recovery on the production database and volume is thereby shown. The hand-off records the URL, build id, rules version and results.
- Every ramp level has a row in the report, including the ones that failed, with the reason; a level whose activity ratio was below target is marked not counted.
- THE LADDER IS READY TO CLIMB, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: deploy/stage.mjs status prints the stage, the workspace's usage and estimated bill, the game's month-to-date and projected spend and every trigger with its current value; every up command and down pass their dry runs against production and print their monthly cost; the move from the combined shape to the split AND the move back pass on the local stack in the pinned image on a live database with flights in progress, with clients that find the new gateway only through the endpoint document (nothing lost by island hash, the freeze reported, every pilot resumed inside the resume window without a reload); the controller scales out and back in on the launch shape of the local stack in dry-run mode, inside the ceiling. If programmes 2 and 3 ran: every step of the stage-up drill has its measured time against its target, and the controller scaled out and back in under load without a restart; if they did not run, the report says so and what the lead must tell the user to run them (the price from ARCHITECTURE 30).
- Railway spend of programme 1 at most $15 beyond the deployment's own bill; programmes 2 and 3 only inside the figure the lead recorded; the report states spend per run and cumulatively.
- No credential in the repository, the image or the client bundle (check-secrets in CI).
SELF-VERIFY: node deploy/stage.mjs status; node deploy/stage.mjs up --to split --dry-run; node deploy/scale.mjs --dry-run --shards 4; node deploy/rollout.mjs --dry-run; npx vitest run bots tests/load; the scripted production and rehearsal checks; the stage-move suite in the pinned image: STACK_NAME=fsp-deploy-loadtest npm run stack -- --compose -- <the suite>.

RULES (docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, binding): (1) Edit only your owned paths; an entry starting with '!' is excluded. A change you need elsewhere is a request file in docs/requests/. The lead owns src/core/contracts (except the parts a brief names), the root configuration (package.json, the lockfile, tsconfig*.json, vite.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, playwright.config.ts, .gitignore), tools/dev, src/core/math, src/core/testing, labs/template and tests/browser/{harness,globalSetup,chromeArgs}.ts. Never run npm install: the dependencies and configuration entries you need are listed under PROVIDED BY THE LEAD in your brief, or are a request. (2) No placeholders, stubs, TODOs or silent fallbacks (CI scans for them); what cannot be finished is stated in the hand-off. workPackages.title: Multi-client acceptance: separate clients under latency, two real browsers, restart and expiry demonstrations, the whole flights
workPackages.brief:
PROJECT: Fable Space Program - a AAA-quality photorealistic true-scale spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge) with one shared, server-authoritative multiplayer universe over the whole solar system. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game (GitHub sshh12/fable-space-program, private, remote origin). BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (both halves; binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (v2; binding; it wins over the research documents and proposals), docs/MIGRATION_V2.md, docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, docs/research/v2/user-decisions.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and: PROMPT.txt "Don't cut corners" and "Verification" of the expansion (your checklist), ARCHITECTURE sections 5, 6.2, 6.4, 13.5, 15.4, 16.1, 16.4 (the local stack and which suite runs on which form of it), 28, 29.1, 31, docs/research/v2/frontend-ux.md section 14, every wave-5 hand-off (net-joint-gate's harness first).

You prove the expansion's verification list with separate clients, and you fix what the proof finds in the simulation, universe and client (you own them this wave: change behaviour only with a failing test that shows the defect; defects in UI, render and server go to docs/requests for the lead and deploy-loadtest). Run against the local stack (ARCHITECTURE 16.4), which needs no cloud resource: npm run stack on host Node processes with the embedded Postgres, in the combined shape that production runs, for the scenario matrix and the browser stories; the compose form in the pinned Linux image only for the restart and recovery demonstrations. Use your own STACK_NAME. ONLY ONE STACK RUNS ON THE MACHINE AT A TIME: every suite of yours runs as npm run stack -- [options] -- <suite>, which holds the one stack slot of heavy.mjs from the moment the stack starts until it has stopped; deploy-loadtest uses the stack too, so hold the slot for one suite at a time and release it between suites (a latency matrix is several runs, not one). PROVIDED BY THE LEAD: npm run stack:client (the production client build, for --page=build) and a globalSetup that uses STACK_URL when the launcher sets it. You never push: the lead moves the release tag, and deploy-loadtest measures only tagged builds, so a simulation fix of yours reaches its ramps only between them. The deployed game is proven by deploy-loadtest and final-gate, not here.

NO SEEDED PROOFS. PROMPT: "no teleporting or cheats". The harness records for every run whether its vessels came from pad spawns on a fresh database or were loaded (seeded); the result table shows it; a seeded run never counts as a completion proof. Required UNSEEDED, from pad spawns, with warp obtained only through the time requests a player has: one rendezvous-and-docking run per latency profile in tests/net, and the station story in tests/acceptance. Other scenarios may start from seeded ships and say so.

A Playwright fixture that opens two Chrome instances with separate profiles against the same server and exposes both pages' window.__test.
