- tests/acceptance, two real browsers at 150 and 300 ms, asserting on WHAT EACH PLAYER SEES (labels, offsets, the single offered action, lamps, mirrored numbers, no reversed outcome): (1) first launch with strangers on neighbouring pads; (2) a station built by three players with a helm hand-over and a staging by a passenger; (3) two friends meeting in lunar orbit, once by meet-at-a-tick and once by in-phase jump; (4) a player back from Saturn finding hubs as echoes with their offers; (5) two strangers who each warped during ascent to different leads end up docked, and in a second run collided, using only offered actions. Story 2 is from pad spawns on a fresh database. Screenshots of both views at the same server tick. Plus: account recovery (park a ship, a clean browser profile, the recovery code, the same ships in My Ships, resume one; the old code no longer works; the ephemeral-profile warning shown before the first ship); first person on a craft without a cabin and each pilot's own view in an assembly; the Credits screen. FRAME TIME IS ASSERTED: at the v2 checkpoints of ARCHITECTURE 29.1 that the stories reach (pad row, docking approach to a three-craft station, map with a crowded census) the measured browser, one at a time under the GPU lock, holds rAF p95 under 16.7 ms and GPU p99 at or under 11 ms.
- Restart and expiry (ARCHITECTURE 28.6), each as a recorded demonstration with before and after state, the restart rows in the pinned image and in BOTH shapes: the rollout during an ascent (the island held until the pilot resumes; the freeze duration), as a deploy overlap of the combined game process with two processes overlapping and as the ordered sequence of the split, and with a changed part definition under parked ships (the decode sweep); THE STAGE MOVE on a live database with a flight in progress, from the combined shape to the split AND from the split back to the combined shape, with clients that are given no address: the endpoint document is changed before the freeze and the pilot resumes on the new gateway inside the 30 s resume window without a reload; in the combined shape a worker isolate killed and the game process killed at the listed moments (at most 250 ms re-run, transitions all or nothing); in the split shape shard kills at the listed moments (flights held for their pilots, the one-key rejoin) and the directory killed with live shards during an ascent with a staging split in the lost batch; Postgres restarted under a live directory; restore from the dump; then, on the host stack, IDLE AND BACK (every client leaves, the graces end, the server is idle with no tick timer and, at the default warm level, one worker isolate and the launch bodies' terrain kept; a fate inside the idle spell is still flown; a returning player deploys and has control no later than on a busy server; once more with idleLevel light: no worker isolate, control within 3 s more) and expiry on the staging rules with an injected wall clock including the assembly rows, the anchor passing, slot accounting and the pressure rule; pad dwell and helm requests surviving a 40 s outage.
- Whole flights (31.4): the Earth-Moon-return mission flown by the scripted pilot as a NetSession client at 150 ms from a launch-window slot with the milestone gates evaluated as objectives on the server; meridian-albatross from a pad to a bound orbit about Mars under private warp; a Neptune arrival at 10,000,000x that ends in a BOUND CAPTURE ELLIPSE on the server's record; the refuelled profile through the socket with two clients (depot launched and parked by one, cruiser docking, propellant transfer, departure); and the same Earth-Moon mission through LocalSession still passing with its golden hash.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Every scenario above passes at every latency profile, or is listed in the hand-off as failing with the measured gap; nothing is skipped silently.
- Docking: both clients report the same port offsets to 1 mm at the event tick; momentum conserved to the server's tolerance; neither client shows a collision, capture or damage before the server's event in any run (assert over event streams).
- Restart: zero ships duplicated or missing (record counts and craft ids); at most 250 ms of flight lost on a kill; assemblies intact.
- Expiry: every row of ARCHITECTURE 15.5 demonstrated with the countdown the client showed matching the removal within 1 s.
- Earth-Moon over the socket: all gates of 31.1 that apply; total corrections above tolerance reported; Mars and Neptune: the server's record is a closed orbit about the body; no event overshoot at the top warp level; the refuelled departure reaches a body beyond the cruiser's unrefuelled reach.
- A one-page result table per PROMPT verification bullet in the hand-off, with the test that proves each and its seeded or unseeded mark; final-gate builds the complete table on it.

The project runs on the Hobby plan with no Serverless service, no hard usage limit and no alert, unless the lead has recorded a move up the ladder in OPEN_QUESTIONS, in which case the stage and its measured cost are stated instead.
5. The repository scan (TODO, FIXME, stub, placeholder outside the allowed simple-body data), the secrets check, the boundary test, the decode corpus of every released build.
6. docs/FINAL_RESULTS.md: ONE ROW PER LINE OF PROMPT.txt (both halves), with the test or demonstration that proves it, where its output is, its result, and for multiplayer proofs whether the run was unseeded. A line without proof is marked NOT DONE and listed first. If the game is not deployed or programme 1 of the load test (ARCHITECTURE 28.7) did not run, the table says NOT DEPLOYED and lists the completion criteria that are therefore unmet; that is reported to the user as a blocker, not as a pass on the local stack. The capacity headline is quoted from the load report with its build id: the measured limit of stage 0 and what broke first, the compute-limited player count at the highest level that ran, the pad limit as the measured per-pad cycle with the 32-pad figure marked derived unless programme 3 ran, the monthly cost idle and at 5 players, and, for stages 2 and 3, either the rehearsed numbers or the plain statement that they are estimates that were not rehearsed, with the scaling path and what it takes to move up.
